title: Generative AI and the Reconfiguration of Creative Works in Short-Form Video Production: A Scoping Review
abstract: Generative AI is changing how short videos are created and is affecting the production, editing and collaboration of content. Existing research is scattered across various fields, such as technology application, creator practice and governance issues, and thus has not achieved all-round coverage of how generative artificial intelligence is changing the creative process and the human-computer relationship. This scoping review examined the prospects, problems and future directions of generative AI in short-video creation. According to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, four databases (ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Google Scholar and Web of Science) were used to systematically identify 13 studies published between 2020 and 2026. Based on the above analysis, generative AI is now used in short-video creation to achieve a joint effort between people and artificial intelligence for generation, selection, verification and modification. From Data-Model Fit to Model-World Fit: A Framework for Integrating Domain Knowledge into Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Machine-learning-based artificial intelligence (AI) systems often perform well in controlled settings but fail when deployed in the real world. These failures stem from a fundamental problem: ML/AI models optimize data-model fit by increasing statistical performance on training data, whereas real-world deployment demands a new paradigm in ML/AI: model-world fit that preserves domain semantics and contextual understanding. We propose a Machine Learning Model-World Fit framework that provides both a conceptual structure for understanding how domain knowledge shapes ML/AI systems and a research roadmap for investigating these relationships. The framework identifies how domain knowledge can be integrated into ML/AI development process via external knowledge representations, such as data, value, process models or domain ontologies. Incorporating external knowledge representations can help overcome three types of knowledge deficiencies in AI: know-what, know-how, and know-why. To illustrate the framework, we apply it to a child welfare placement case, a domain where contextual understanding is critical and statistical accuracy is an insufficient evaluation criterion. title: Bringing a HASS lens to work-integrated learning: Australian contexts, challenges, opportunities
abstract: This paper examines Work-integrated Learning (WIL) as a pedagogy within Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences (HASS) learning and teaching. It examines WIL as an important strategy for ensuring that the university is contemporary, connected, and engaged with the realities of the rapidly changing nature of work. WIL has the capacity to enable greater mobility between the university and strategic partners – encompassing industry, business, community, not-for-profit, cultural and governmental bodies, and even other areas of the educational institution – and can demonstrate the value of HASS both to partners and to students themselves. This article positions HASS disciplines in relation to the contemporary Australian higher education sector’s employability agenda, argues for the value of these disciplines to employers, the workforce and to the future of work, and offers recommendations for designing contemporary curricula using the pedagogy of WIL as seen through the lens of HASS disciplinary learning. title: Faculty and Staff Program on Generative AI and the Construction of an AI ‐Assisted Knowledge‐Sharing Website
abstract: This study examines a faculty and staff program on generative AI at the Hokkaido University of Science and proposes a reusable AI‐assisted workflow for developing a knowledge‐sharing website. The program addressed fundamental concepts, applications, and ethical considerations for participants from diverse backgrounds. A total of 120 individuals attended, and 83 valid responses were obtained. Quantitative findings demonstrated a good understanding and perceived usefulness, while qualitative feedback revealed increased motivation, broader perspectives, and heightened ethical awareness. Negative feedback highlighted concerns regarding security, time constraints, technical challenges, and mismatches with prior knowledge of the subject. To facilitate ongoing learning, a knowledge‐sharing website was created by transforming handwritten discussion notes into structured digital content using AI. Usage logs indicated relatively strong initial access; however, short engagement times suggest the need for enhanced usability and interactivity. title: Artificial intelligence for radiographic assessment of peri-implant marginal bone loss: a systematic review and meta-analysis of model performance
abstract: Artificial intelligence has been applied to dental radiographic interpretation, including assessment of peri-implant marginal bone loss and peri-implantitis-related bone defects. Most available evidence has focused on lesion detection; quantitative measurement, severity grading, and clinical applicability have been less consistently examined. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the performance of AI models for radiographic assessment of peri-implant marginal bone loss and related bone defects. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception to 25 May 2026. Google Scholar, reference lists, and citation tracking were also used to identify additional records. English-language original studies were eligible if they used AI-based methods to assess peri-implant marginal bone loss, peri-implant bone-level changes, peri-implantitis-related radiographic bone defects, or severity grading on dental radiographic images. title: Implementation Science in the Pharmaceutical Industry: Why we Know which Innovations Work but Still Cannot Implement Them - A Comparative Review of the United States, the European Union, and International Regulatory Contexts
abstract: Even though there have been major scientific developments in the fields of pharmaceutical analytical chemistry, manufacturing science, and regulatory science over the last twenty years, the incorporation of validated innovations into routine industrial practice remains slow, irregular, and incomplete. Although Quality by Design (QbD), Process Analytical Technology (PAT), continuous manufacturing (CM), Real-Time Release Testing (RTRT), and artificial intelligence (AI) are backed by strong scientific bases and have clear regulatory routes, their adoption differs greatly from product to product, facility to facility, and region to region. This structured narrative review uses implementation science, a field that systematically examines methods for integrating evidence into everyday practice, to examine innovations in pharmaceutical analytical and manufacturing processes. The review brings together the regulatory environments in the United States (21 CFR Parts 210/211, the FDA Emerging Technology Program, Quality Management Maturity), in the European Union (EudraLex Volume 4, Annex 1 on sterile manufacturing, the reform of EU pharmaceutical legislation), and in international frameworks

title: The Editor's Challenge: Safeguarding Scientific Integrity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: In today’s changing time, Artificial intelligence (AI) has already transformed academic writing by improving language, summarizing literature, and assisting manuscript preparation. The editorial challenge of the AI era is no longer detecting copied words; it is distinguishing genuine scientific thinking from convincingly generated text. Technology may assist scientific writing, but only integrity can produce science worthy of publication.

title: The Pocket Tutor Has a Price: Scaffolding Self-Paced Learning with AI
abstract: The dominant narrative casts large language models (LLMs) as a low-cost realization of Bloom’s two-sigma tutor: patient, always available, personalizing at scale. Self-paced online learning, the fastest-growing segment of higher and continuing education and the backbone of the data-science workforce pipeline, is where this promise is most attractive and most dangerous. Through an integrative synthesis of cognitive science, learning theory, computing-education evidence, and the economics of services, we argue that self-paced settings strip away the implicit scaffolding of the classroom (instructor presence, peers, accountability, ambient feedback), so unguided LLM access defaults to cognitive offloading, metacognitive disengagement, and fragmented learning that erodes durable competence. Recent large-scale evidence, including a survey of over ninety-five thousand undergraduates that found sharply elevated failure rates in introductory computing, is consistent with this. title: AlphaFold 3: Architecture and Applications in Protein–Ligand Complex Prediction
abstract: The interaction between proteins and ligands is the core mechanism of biological activities and drug development. In traditional experimental methods, there are a series of problems such as long research cycles, high costs, and limited precision. In the rapid way of artificial intelligence (AI) era, AI tools have driven the progress of biological science. Therefore, this article focuses on elaborating on the new AI tool Alphafold to analyze the three-dimensional spatial structure of proteins. Especially Alphafold3(AF3), which adds diffusion algorithms, confidence assessment units, and the Pairformer module to the original AI model and simplifies the calculation steps, has achieved a revolutionary leap from single atom or protein homologous sequence pairing output to position pairing output between nucleic acids - proteins and peptide residues. It has realized the all-round design of protein-ligand complexes throughout the process. title: Scale-free Niche Construction: expanding agent-microenvironment co-development to unconventional substrates
abstract: Niche construction emphasizes the active aspect of life forms that alter their environment via feedback loops in which that environment inevitably changes their behavior, structure, and future evolution. We argue that this powerful dynamic is general, extending far beyond typical applications in ecology and evolutionary biology. We explain how niche construction extends the scope of classical predictive and control loops beyond the nervous system and organism-level. Examples from cognitive science, psychopathology, cell and developmental biology, cancer biology, robotics, and AI illustrate how agents use living and non-living aspects of their microenvironment as a scratchpad, allowing active long-term memory that supports cohesion of agency over time. Niche construction enables "offloading" to the environment (externalizing) various cognitive operations, including planning, problem solving, and social coordination. We also discuss niche construction an example of the plasticity of the machine/data mapping, enabling analysis of systems from the perspective of the patterns within excitable media (agential data). title: Artificial intelligence in radiographic quantification and severity assessment of peri‐implant marginal bone loss: A systematic review
abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose To critically assess artificial intelligence (AI)‐based radiographic models for quantitative measurement, localization/detection, segmentation/keypoints, diagnostic classification, and severity or morphology assessment of peri‐implant marginal bone loss (MBL) and peri‐implantitis‐related bone defects. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and reference lists were searched from inception through August 11, 2026. Eligible original studies evaluated AI‐based radiographic assessment of existing dental implants. Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies‐3 (QUADAS‐3) was applied at the prespecified estimate level for diagnostic/image‐analysis studies and PROBAST for the prediction‐model study. Results A total of 1485 records were identified, and 17 studies were included. Fourteen reported localization/detection outcomes, six segmentation/keypoint outcomes, 10 severity/morphology outcomes, 12 diagnostic/classification outcomes, and six direct AI–clinician comparisons; categories overlapped. title: Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence and Their Relationship with Positive Youth Development Among Spanish Undergraduates
abstract: It is important to understand young people’s attitudes towards artificial intelligence (AI) in order to ensure responsible use. Positive Youth Development (PYD) has been identified as a protective factor against risks related to digital technologies. Further research is needed concerning attitudes toward AI from a strengths-based perspective. This study aimed to examine these attitudes and their relationships with the 5Cs of the PYD model among undergraduates. A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025. A sample of 407 university students (63.1% women, Mage = 21.93), enrolled at 10 universities in the region of Andalusia (Spain) completed the PYD-SF and the AIAS-4 measures. The students in Science, Engineering, and Architecture degrees showed the most positive attitude scores, whereas those in Arts and Humanities scored the lowest. The hypothesized positive association between the 5Cs and attitudes toward AI was partially supported. Competence and Confidence were positively associated with these attitudes, while Character showed an inverse relationship, suggesting that students with higher moral awareness may remain particularly vigilant about ethical risks and social inequaliti

title: Artificial intelligence and computational prediction models for risk stratification, treatment response, and outcomes in colorectal cancer: a narrative review
abstract: Purpose To critically evaluate, within a decision-centred framework, the clinical readiness of artificial-intelligence (AI) and computational prediction models used for risk stratification, treatment-response assessment, and outcome prediction in colorectal cancer (CRC), while distinguishing tumour site, intended clinical decision, assessment time point, and validation level, and identifying the gap between predictive performance and clinical impact. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science were searched for English-language studies published from January 2010 through 31 May 2026; ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, reference lists, and forward citation tracking were used as supplementary sources. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted design, endpoint, data modality, unit of analysis, validation, calibration, decision analysis, workflow evaluation, accessibility, and clinical-impact evidence. Study-level methodological features were assessed separately from task-level translational readiness. title: Geospatial Artificial Intelligence in Precision Agriculture: A Systematic Review of Applications, Multimodal Data Integration, and Decision Support
abstract: Geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI) offers opportunities to translate heterogeneous agricultural observations into site-specific management decisions. This systematic review synthesizes literature published in 2019–2026, identified through Scopus, Web of Science, and supplementary searches, to examine applications, multimodal data integration, and decision support in precision agriculture. The narrative synthesis indicates a shift from isolated mapping and prediction toward integrated workflows combining satellite and UAV imagery, field sensors, weather, soil, and management records. Reported benefits include improved yield prediction, earlier stress and disease detection, more detailed soil mapping, and more targeted irrigation and input use. However, farming yield, environmental, and economic gains remain dependent on local conditions and operational validation. A central finding is that georeferenced data alone do not ensure genuinely geospatial AI: reliable workflows must address spatial dependence, scale mismatch, transferability, and uncertainty. Interpretability and integration into farm operations are equally important for actionable recommendations. Adoption remains

title: Beyond Behavioral Intention: A Context-Validated Framework for Meaningful Use of PictureThis AI in Ugandan Public Universities
abstract: Purpose: This study validated and refined a context-specific framework explaining meaningful use behavior of PictureThis artificial intelligence (AI) for plant identification among undergraduate students in Ugandan public universities. Unlike an earlier analysis of predictors of behavioral intention from the same doctoral study, this article centres on the intention-to-use gap, actual academic engagement, mediation, moderation, and framework refinement. Materials and Methods: A positivist, quantitative, cross-sectional correlational survey was conducted with 477 biological and agricultural science students from Makerere, Busitema, Gulu, and Kabale universities. After at least 30 days of guided PictureThis use, participants completed an adapted UTAUT2 questionnaire. Use behavior was operationalized as user cognitive absorption and deep-structure usage. Measurement and structural models, mediation, and moderation were evaluated with partial least squares structural equation modelling in SmartPLS 4. Findings: The seven UTAUT2 predictors explained 62.7% of behavioral intention, but intention explained only 0.7% of meaningful use and did not significantly predict it (β = .081, p = .252)

title: Simulación de Partícula 64D mediante MREI: Validación de Capacidad del Paradigma Post-Clásico/ DUQUEANA CORE
abstract: Este trabajo presenta la simulación computacional de una estructura de partícula en 64 dimensiones utilizando el Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI) del paradigma post-clásico. A diferencia de los enfoques clásicos que requieren escalado masivo de recursos (GB-TB de RAM), esta simulación demuestra que la verificación estructural determinista permite modelar geometrías de alta dimensionalidad con eficiencia extrema (~6 KB RAM de ejecución). Los resultados validan la capacidad del motor MREI para preservar invariantes geométricas en espacios multidimensionales, estableciendo un precedente para simulaciones de física teórica, teoría de cuerdas y geometría algebraica avanzada. La arquitectura post-clásica, fundamentada en organización geométrica en lugar de correlación estadística, demuestra ser viable para problemas de frontera previamente considerados inaccesibles para hardware clásico. title: An Autonomous Agentic Query Framework with MCP Tools and Modernized NIST SRD-46 for Accelerating Aqueous Speciation Analysis
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) could automate reasoning over structured scientific databases in chemistry and materials science, but this requires purpose-built agentic architectures, not simply better models. We present an agentic workflow for systematically querying and extracting data from the NIST Standard Reference Database 46 (SRD-46) to perform autonomous speciation and thermodynamic analysis, with three contributions: (1) a hierarchical toolset, served by Model Context Protocol (MCP) framework, which converts natural-language scientific questions into validated SQL over a database enriched with canonical chemical identifiers, equilibrium-reaction maps, and fingerprint-similarity matrices; (2) an induction-deduction-validation reasoning loop with compactors that preserve key chemical context across multi-turn sessions under dynamic memory limits within the same session; and (3) a soft time/turn-budget hook that maintains coherent reasoning within resource constraints. The resulting framework is LLM-agnostic and spans queries from direct lookups to cross-species comparisons to open-ended tasks like estimating unknown Fe complexation constants and selecting ligands for acidic Fe

title: Replication Radar
abstract: Replication Radar turns the OpenAIRE Graph into a ranked replication queue and adds the signals the Graph cannot hold: whether a claim has been independently checked (with the verdict, read live from the Science Live nanopublication network) and whether the software behind it is reusable (the fair-software.eu recommendations plus RSE good-practice signals, computed live from GitHub, Software Heritage and Zenodo). It is a static web app and an MCP server for AI agents, designed to run alongside the OpenAIRE MCP.

title: Mamba-TransQR v1.0.1: PeerJ Reproducibility Documentation Update
abstract: Mamba-TransQR v1.0.1 is a documentation-only reproducibility update prepared for the PeerJ Computer Science AI Application submission. The README, reproduction instructions, citation metadata, repository metadata, and reproducibility documentation were improved. The model architecture, trained checkpoints, dataset lineage, quantitative results, figures, tables, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged from v1.0.0. Frozen scientific provenance remains associated with v1.0.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21913175). Version 1.0.1 does not report new experimental performance. Source code and associated repository documentation are provided under the MIT License. Dataset and checkpoint/model-weight licenses are not separately documented.

title: Responsible Innovation and Gender Inequality in Artificial Intelligence: Workforce Inclusion and Social Sustainability
abstract: Description Replication Package: Responsible Innovation and Gender Inequality in Artificial Intelligence: Workforce Inclusion and Social Sustainability This replication package accompanies the study “Responsible Innovation and Gender Inequality in Artificial Intelligence: Workforce Inclusion and Social Sustainability.” The study examines gender inequality in the artificial intelligence (AI) and data science workforce using four consecutive waves of the Kaggle Machine Learning and Data Science Survey (2018–2021), comprising 87,945 respondents from more than 50 countries. The analysis examines gender differences across workforce participation, age, educational attainment, occupational roles, coding and machine learning experience, annual compensation, industry sectors, and geographic representation. The study is guided by responsible innovation theory, with inclusion as the principal responsible innovation dimension implicated by the empirical findings. STEM Pipeline Theory is used as an explanatory mechanism for understanding how gender disparities may accumulate across successive stages of workforce participation. title: Data Pipeline Architecture for the Integration of Technology and Artificial Intelligence in the Competencies of the Future Manager
abstract: This study addresses the need to update professional profiles in higher education in response to the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data science. The objective of this research was to implement a computational data pipeline based on an Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) approach to automatically assess the technological competencies demanded by the labor market. Using this algorithmic workflow implemented in Python, data collected from a probabilistic sample of 52 companies, determined through the finite population sampling formula with a 5% margin of error, were processed. The results showed that 88.4% of employers prioritized Business Intelligence and Advanced Analytics, while 84.6% emphasized competencies related to Artificial Intelligence-driven process automation. Furthermore, the analysis of the historical enrollment records of 3,149 students confirmed the institutional operational feasibility and provided the technical evidence that supported the official approval of the proposed Digital Management and Business Intelligence specialization at the Technological Institute of Pachuca. title: Disturbance Observer-based Model Predictive Control for a Twin Rotor MIMO System
abstract: This paper presents a disturbance observer–based model predictive control strategy for the position regulation of a twin rotor MIMO system (TRMS). The nonlinear dynamics of the TRMS are first rewritten as an uncertain linear time invariant (LTI) system with additive disturbances. An extended state observer (ESO) is then designed to estimate both the system states and the lumped disturbance term. Using these estimates, a composite model predictive control law is formulated to achieve robust tracking performance of the desired positions of the TRMS. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme. title: Quantum Vision Ai For Pediatric Urological Screening Using Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: Pediatric urological disorders require timely recognition to reduce the risk of persistent functional, reproductive, and psychosocial consequences, yet screening still depends heavily on clinician-led visual examination. This study develops and evaluates Quantum Vision AI, a child-safe intelligent screening platform that integrates non-invasive medical imaging, Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and clinical decision support. A Design Science Research approach combined with experimental quantitative validation was used to construct the prototype. Standardized pediatric external-genital images were preprocessed and analyzed through a hybrid quantum-classical architecture in which classical vision models extracted anatomical features, quantum circuits enhanced feature representation, and explainability methods visualized diagnostically relevant regions. The proposed platform consistently outperformed the conventional convolutional, EfficientNetV2, and Vision Transformer baselines used in the study, while its attention maps concentrated on clinically meaningful anatomical structures and expert reviewers reported favorable usability and diagnostic rel

title: GitHub or Codeberg? Choosing the Right Platform for developing and managing Code or Research Software
abstract: GitHub or Codeberg? Choosing the Right Platform for developing and managing Code or Research Software Presented on 15-09-2026 at Radboud University GitHub has become a widely-used platform for managing code, collaborating on software projects, and supporting reproducible research. As the platform is owned by Microsoft, and recently started training its AI models on user data without users’ consent, growing attention to digital sovereignty and research integrity has prompted researchers and institutions to reflect whether alternatives are available. One such alternative could be Codeberg, a European non-profit platform that offers many of the same core functionalities as GitHub while operating under a community-driven governance model. In this lecture, we will explore the similarities and differences between GitHub and Codeberg, discuss the broader concept of digital sovereignty, and consider the pros and cons of both platforms. Whether you are already using GitHub or Codeberg, or simply interested in the future of research infrastructure, this session will provide valuable insights and an opportunity for discussion. title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Herbal Formulation Development: From Phytochemical Intelligence to Predictive Nanodelivery and Precision Phytotherapy
abstract: Herbal medicines constitute a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules and remain important components of traditional and complementary healthcare systems. However, the development of reproducible pharmaceutical formulations from herbal materials is complicated by variability in botanical identity, geographical origin, cultivation, harvesting, processing, extraction, phytochemical composition, and storage, all of which contribute to batch-to-batch variation in biological activity and formulation performance. title: Mining, wildlife and habitat in India: a systematic review of impacts, sustainable practices, reclamation technologies and governance, with special reference to Odisha
abstract: This systematic review will synthesise peer-reviewed evidence published between 1 January 2006 and 21 September 2026 on four linked questions about mining in India: (1) the impacts of mining on forest and land use, wildlife and habitat connectivity, water and soil, human health and livelihoods, with special reference to Odisha; (2) sustainable mining practices and reclamation technologies, globally and in India; (3) the tools and technologies used to monitor mine restoration, including satellite remote sensing, UAVs, LiDAR, machine learning and phytoremediation; and (4) India's regulatory and governance framework, assessed against the mitigation hierarchy of avoid, minimise, restore and offset. Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection will be searched using a pre-specified Boolean strategy, supplemented by backward and forward citation chasing; international comparative studies will be recorded separately as identified through other methods. Eligible studies are peer-reviewed, English-language journal articles or scholarly books that report an explicit mining exposure and a relevant outcome or intervention. title: A Systematic Review and Unified Framework for Predictive Maintenance in the Railway Domain
abstract: Predictive maintenance has become an important strategy for improving asset reliability and safety, particularly with the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into maintenance processes. In the railway domain, where maintenance activities can account for up to 40% of the overall budget allocated across the V-cycle of rolling stock development, the adoption of smart maintenance strategies is increasingly important. However, an integrated understanding of predictive maintenance approaches across the railway domain remains lacking. This study provides an in-depth review of predictive maintenance research in the railway domain through a PRISMA-guided systematic search of three major scientific databases: Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect. A total of 61 full-text articles were retained and analyzed in detail. The reviewed studies are synthesized according to their methodological approaches, namely data-driven, model-based, and hybrid approaches, and their distribution across railway subsystems is examined. title: Problem Sheets - Artificial Intelligence in the Life Sciences - Ruhr University Bochum
abstract: This record contains five problem sheets from the lecture Artificial Intelligence in the Life Sciences, held in the winter term 2025/26 at the Faculty of Biology and Biotechnology, Ruhr University Bochum. The exercises take students from classical machine learning to modern deep learning and explainable AI, and many of them use life-science examples such as microscopy, histopathology, genomics and medical imaging. Topics include: Sheet 1: k-means and single-linkage clustering, decision trees and Shannon entropy, bagging and random forests Sheet 2: component trees, Otsu thresholding, PCA, Kullback–Leibler divergence, t-SNE and convolution operations Sheet 3: image filters (Sobel, Gaussian), fully connected networks with forward and backward passes, U-Net and ResNet Sheet 4: dropout, self-attention, scaled dot-product and multi-head attention, positional encoding and transformers Sheet 5: saliency maps, class activation maps (CAM), attention-based interpretability in multiple instance learning (MIL), and Shapley values Each sheet is provided as LaTeX source (exam document class) with points for every subtask and a grading table. Sheets 4 and 5 require XeLaTeX.

title: Reporting and Control of Color Stimuli in Emotion and Cognition Experiments: A Systematic Methodological Review
abstract: This systematic methodological review will audit reporting, stated control procedures and current availability of color-stimulus information in eligible human emotion and cognition experiments using two-dimensional electronic displays. It will use experiment/configuration-level evidence and 26 item-specific rules, separating information sufficiency, implementation, accessibility and applicability. It will not pool behavioral effect sizes or infer replication success from reporting completeness. The planned core strategy is the tested W6 across Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection and single APA PsycINFO; the eligibility start remains 2000, with WoS's observed 2010-onward coverage reported as a limitation. Full formal searching, complete export, deduplication, dual screening, extraction and synthesis are planned after registration. The initial common eligibility cutoff is the Asia/Shanghai date of the first formal core search, with the three initial searches completed within seven days. title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Herbal Formulation Development: From Phytochemical Intelligence to Predictive Nanodelivery and Precision Phytotherapy
abstract: Herbal medicines constitute a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules and remain important components of traditional and complementary healthcare systems. However, the development of reproducible pharmaceutical formulations from herbal materials is complicated by variability in botanical identity, geographical origin, cultivation, harvesting, processing, extraction, phytochemical composition, and storage, all of which contribute to batch-to-batch variation in biological activity and formulation performance. title: AI-Driven Digital Marketing in Higher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of College Choice Intention Research, 2022–2026
abstract: Abstract : This study maps the intellectual structure of research on AI-driven digital marketing in higher education and its relationship to college choice intention, where the literatures on AI acceptance and student recruitment have developed separately. Methodology A bibliometric analysis of 430 Scopus-indexed articles (2022–2026) was conducted in VOS viewer. A three-block Boolean search combined digital marketing, artificial intelligence, higher education and college choice constructs, analysed through network, overlay and density visualisations. Findings Output grew from 11 articles in 2022 to 197 in 2025, with 76.28 per cent of the corpus appearing in the final two years. Social Sciences (36.5%) and Computer Science (17.3%) dominate. “Artificial intelligence”, “behavioural intention” and “technology acceptance model” form the conceptual core, whereas enrolment intention, student recruitment and digital trust remain peripheral. China leads output (24.4%), indicating a shift in knowledge production towards Asia and the Middle East. Research limitations Reliance on a single database and on English-language articles may under-represent developments first reported in conference pr

title: AI resistance and epistemic agency: toward a relational framework for democratic and human-centered AI governance
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly mediates communication, interpretation, decision-making, and knowledge production, raising questions about how computational systems acquire epistemic authority. At the same time, resistance to AI is emerging across educational, creative, infrastructural, professional, and civic settings. This conceptual paper examines what such resistance reveals about the distribution and contestability of epistemic authority in AI-mediated environments. Drawing on Science and Technology Studies, critical AI studies, AI ethics, political philosophy, and epistemic theory, it extends emerging accounts of AI-mediated epistemic capture by connecting them to epistemic agency, resistance, and governance . Epistemic capture is conceptualized as a gradual and relational process through which interpretive authority can become increasingly organized around computational systems and difficult to contest. The paper develops a typology encompassing quiet refusal, epistemic, infrastructural, educational, creative, and decolonial resistance, together with reclamation, while emphasizing that resistance is not inherently emancipatory or epistemically beneficial.

QUESTION ASSETS
abstract: QUESTION ASSETS What Civilization Has Not Yet Answered, Yet Future Generations Should Continue to Ask A Civilizational Aesthetics of Questions, Possibility, Memory, and Handoff QUESTION ASSETS explores a simple but far-reaching idea: A civilization is not measured only by how many answers it preserves. It may also be measured by how many meaningful questions it enables future generations to continue asking. The book begins from a distinction: Question ≠ Question Asset. Not every unanswered question becomes a civilizational asset. A Question Asset is a question capable of preserving future intellectual possibility. It may remain valuable because it continues to generate research, reveal hidden assumptions, expose new variables, connect previously separated fields, inspire new methods, or help later generations reinterpret problems that earlier generations could not yet solve. This leads to the central proposition of the book: Answers preserve knowledge. Questions preserve possibility. Knowledge tells us what has already been learned. Questions preserve what may still become possible. In this sense, an unanswered question is not always a deficiency. Sometimes it is an inheritance. QU

title: Can recovered phosphorus fertilisers replace mineral phosphorus? Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: This protocol covers a systematic review and meta-analysis of recovered phosphorus fertilisers in agricultural crop systems. Two estimands will be analysed separately: recovered phosphorus versus conventional mineral phosphorus at a comparable elemental-phosphorus dose ratio of 0.90 to 1.10, and recovered phosphorus versus zero-phosphorus or no-added-phosphorus controls. Harvestable yield is the primary outcome; biomass, plant phosphorus uptake and phosphorus-use efficiency are separate secondary outcome families. Eligible settings include field experiments and soil-based greenhouse or pot studies; hydroponic and inert-substrate systems are excluded. Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched. Scholar Gateway and the Scopus AI discovery interface were used only for supplementary discovery, and every lead was checked in the classical bibliographic sources; CAB Abstracts was unavailable and was not searched. Pilot searches, provisional author screening and limited full-text feasibility checks preceded registration. Final eligibility validation, retrieval, extraction, risk-of-bias assessment and quantitative synthesis will occur after registration.

title: AI for Verification and Validation of Safety-Critical Systems: reproducibility package (bibliometric data, code, and AVAF coding, 2016–2026)
abstract: Reproducibility package for a bibliometric science-mapping study of artificial intelligence for the verification and validation (V&V) of safety-critical systems (2016–2026), and for the AI-Verification Assurance Framework (AVAF). Contains the raw Scopus and Web of Science exports, a single commented R script reproducing the full pipeline (import, merge, de-duplication, programmatic eligibility screening with per-reason exclusion counts, controlled thesaurus and stop-terms, co-word network, consensus community partition over 30 restarts, sensitivity/ARI grid, thematic map, and trend topics), the derived outputs (PRISMA counts, descriptor tables, cluster and sensitivity results, figures), the AVAF coding workbook (codebook, coded subsample, and intra-coder test–retest reliability), a README, and R session information. The analysed corpus comprises 425 documents (search date: 4 July 2026). The random seed is fixed for deterministic reproduction.

title: Evaluation Results Master Thesis Pablo Arteaga
abstract: Evaluation Results: BPM-based guidelines for personal contexts This dataset contains the responses of the user evaluation carried out for the master's thesis From Everyday Problems to Structured Solutions: BPM Guidelines for Personal Contexts (Pablo Arteaga Bravo, MSc Business Informatics, Utrecht University, 2026). The evaluation is described in Section 3.4 of the thesis, and its results are reported in Chapter 5. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22882601 License: CC BY 4.0 Contact: Pablo Arteaga Bravo, p.arteagabravo@students.uu.nl Study design Participants completed a pre-test questionnaire and received a participant guide describing six BPM-based guidelines: As-Is / To-Be, 5 Whys, Product-Based Design, Value-Added Analysis, MCDA and Knock-Out. They then applied the guidelines to situations in their own lives for one week, extended by a second week if no guideline had been applied, and completed a post-test questionnaire. title: Constructing AI power: anthropomorphising imaginaries of generative AI by AI companies
abstract: Abstract In descriptions of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), companies often anthropomorphise their innovations by attributing human-associated characteristics or capabilities to them, e.g. intelligence, understanding or reasoning. I argue that anthropomorphism can become a structuring part of sociotechnical imaginaries—visions of desirable futures attainable through advances in science and technology. While imaginaries of GenAI have been addressed in existing research, both the connection between anthropomorphism and imaginaries as well as the perspective of AI companies as creators of hegemonic imaginaries remain understudied. Drawing on a qualitative content analysis of 35 documents from OpenAI, Meta and Mistral AI, I explored which anthropomorphising imaginaries are employed by AI companies and how anthropomorphism constructs the technology as powerful in future societies. The analysis reveals that companies anthropomorphise GenAI both in terms of content and language, creating three anthropomorphising imaginaries. title: Jev/System One model comes short where Palantir comes short
abstract: This document archives an AI-assisted analytical dialogue examining the relationship among TypeSafe AI’s Jev/System One models, Palantir’s ontology-centered operational architecture, ontology-based agent-governance proposals associated with Frank Coyle, and the Bridge360 Metatheory Model. The central question is whether replacing open-ended natural-language generation with typed, probabilistic, schema-constrained machine inference removes—or merely relocates—the governance problems associated with ontology-driven operational systems. The discussion distinguishes Jev/System One from Palantir at the architectural level. Jev is treated as a typed probabilistic inference substrate whose outputs are constrained by predefined schemas, probabilities, confidence measures, and programmer-written workflow logic, whereas Palantir’s Ontology explicitly integrates objects, properties, links, actions, functions, permissions, workflow, and operational write-back. title: THE SHUOHUA FUNCTIONS OF THE UNIVERSE
abstract: THE SHUOHUA FUNCTIONS OF THE UNIVERSE E19-P12 Side Story A Speculative Companion to the Universe-Level Shuohua Extension HIGHLY SPECULATIVE THE SHUOHUA FUNCTIONS OF THE UNIVERSE is a mathematical and scientific companion to E19-P12, THE UNIVERSE-LEVEL SHUOHUA EXTENSION. The main E19-P12 volume asks whether any universe-scale interpretation of Shuohua deserves to become a serious research question. This companion asks the next question: If universe-scale updating can be formalized at all, what might the first candidate family of functions look like? The book does not claim that the universe has a hidden Shuohua function. It does not propose a new established law of physics. It does not treat mathematical notation as evidence. Instead, it deliberately converts speculative language into candidate mathematical objects so that those ideas can be examined, compared, constrained, rejected, or eventually refined. title: Global research trends and knowledge mapping of artificial intelligence in triple negative breast cancer: a ten-year bibliometric analysis
abstract: This study aims to systematically delineate the global research landscape, developmental trajectory, and emerging hotspots of artificial intelligence (AI) in triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) between 2015 and 2025, thereby providing a scientific basis and strategic pathways for the advancement of precision oncology. Relevant literature on artificial intelligence in the field of TNBC from 2015 to 2025 was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Tableau were used for bibliometric and visualization analysis. The contribution characteristics of countries, institutions, and authors, as well as the co-occurrence patterns of keywords, were systematically analyzed. The analysis of highly cited references is used to evaluate important achievements accumulated in the research field over the medium to long term. The study included 320 articles. Publication volume reached an inflection point of upward growth in 2022, peaking at 104 articles in 2025, accompanied by a simultaneous acceleration in annual citations. title: The Connected Threat Picture: A Graded Assessment of AI Risk from Cognitive Influence to Autonomous Action
abstract: Assessments of AI risk often separate present harms from catastrophic futures and treat each danger in isolation. This paper sets out a connected threat picture in which persuasive systems, autonomous agents, adversarial actors, concentrated infrastructure and economic disruption interact with the capacity of people and institutions to respond. It brings cognitive security together with governance, corporate power, physical security, biological misuse, labour and welfare. Each specified claim is assessed against its evidence, exposure and horizon; severity, confidence, likelihood, reversibility and intervention capacity remain distinct. A developer's September 2026 incident report documents misuse in cyber operations, influence campaigns and weapons development, while its simulated drone-development case does not establish field deployment of a lethal autonomous weapon. The paper examines industry warnings about autonomy and superintelligence, the possible pathway from economic grievance to political violence, bounded biohybrid demonstrations and the critical skills on which cognitive defence depends. title: Cross-Scale Biomedical Data Construction and Representation in the Foundation Model Era: A Survey
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) pre-trained on biological, biomedical, and clinical corpora are reshaping life-science research across protein structure prediction, single-cell analysis, computational pathology, and clinical decision support. Surveys are model-centric, cataloging architectures while treating data as secondary and single-scale. Biological FMs integrate sequences, structures, molecular interactions, omics profiles, images, and clinical records across scales and time. These corpora are sparsely paired, unevenly curated, and dependent on ontologies and measurement protocols, so data construction and alignment determine generalizability. We focus on data construction, representation, and cross-scale alignment. We introduce a three-dimensional tensor index spanning biological scale (molecular to population/cohort, plus cross-scale alignment), data operation (construction to service), and technical era (curated knowledge to foundation models). title: Grey Matters: Strategic Approaches to Managing Non-Traditional Research Outputs
abstract: The German National Library of Science and Technology (TIB) maintains extensive collections of grey literature – technical reports, conference proceedings, dissertations, and other non-commercially published research outputs – that require specialised approaches to acquisition, preservation, and access. This paper examines TIB's strategic approach to managing these non-traditional research outputs (NTROs), using the German Research Reports collection (Deutsche Forschungsberichte, DtF) as a case study. We discuss the implementation of TIB's e-preferred strategy, persistent challenges around accessibility and discoverability, and ongoing efforts – including collaboration with OpenAlex and the AI search platform ORKG Ask – to improve the visibility of grey literature on national and international discovery platforms.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmacy Education: Opportunities, Challenges and Future Directions
abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare and pharmacy practice, creating a need to prepare future pharmacists for AI-assisted professional environments. English-language articles published between September 2023 and February 2026 were eligible for inclusion, and the literature search was conducted between April 2026 and June 2026. Studies addressing AI applications in pharmacy education, AI-assisted learning, curriculum integration, students’ knowledge and perceptions, educational technologies, ethical considerations, and future directions were included. title: Can algal bioinputs replace mineral fertilisers? Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: This protocol covers a systematic review and meta-analysis of algal, microalgal and cyanobacterial bioinputs used to reduce or replace conventional mineral fertiliser in agricultural crop systems. The primary comparison is a reduced mineral-fertiliser regime plus an identified algal bioinput versus the full-rate mineral-fertiliser comparator. Harvestable yield is the primary outcome, evaluated with a prespecified non-inferiority interpretation; biomass, nutrient uptake, nutrient-use efficiency and soil outcomes are analysed separately. Eligible bioinputs include living microalgae, whole or dried biomass, residues, extracts or hydrolysates, cyanobacterial inocula, macroalgal products, algal digestates and mixed formulations whose algal component is identifiable. Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched. Scholar Gateway and the Scopus AI discovery interface were used only for supplementary discovery, with all leads verified in authoritative sources; CAB Abstracts was unavailable and was not searched. Pilot searches and provisional author screening preceded registration. Final eligibility validation, full-text retrieval, extraction, risk-of-bias assessment and synthesis

title: Designing ethical AI literacy across secondary to graduate STEM pathways: ensuring cross-disciplinary outcomes and workforce alignment
abstract: Rapid adoption of generative AI in STEM courses has created an urgent need for practical, ethical AI literacy that students can carry from high school into college and beyond. In this Perspective, we make the case for a cross-disciplinary approach to AI literacy and present a skills progression table that aligns core outcomes with typical academic and professional levels (high school, early undergraduate, advanced undergraduate, graduate, and workplace). We focus on six core areas: (i) attribution and citation, (ii) bias awareness and mitigation, (iii) privacy and data handling, (iv) safety and environmental care, (v) community impact and fairness, and (vi) compliance and readiness for audit. We frame AI-related classroom practice as a balancing act, on one side, clear benefits (faster drafting, coding support, and broader access), and on the other, real risks (bias, privacy leaks, over-reliance, and academic integrity concerns). To ground our Perspective in STEM broadly, we offer guidance with suggested steps and actions, grading cues, rural/low-bandwidth adaptations, and links to workforce expectations. The result was an asymmetric measurement event: authors kept the numbers and lost the norm. SSRN's counters did not become meaningless; they became unreadable. Every download count became a number without a scale. This article argues that the question "What does 7 downloads mean?" is scientifically ill-posed until a paper's reference class is specified. Does Writing "This Paper Does Not" Evade Refutation, or Aim It? ── 516 of 524 papers carry a scope note, with 3649 declarations ending in a negation ── by word family, 978 narrow the target while 728 shrink the claim itself ── [Paper 526]
abstract: This corpus places a scope note beginning “this paper does not” in almost every paper. What this paper shows is that those notes fall into two groups whose effects are opposite: one aims the refutation, the other shrinks the claim. Which is better is not adjudicated here; the numbers are given and the judgement is returned to the author. No new theorem or law is claimed. Scope of this paper (scope note): No new theorem or law is claimed──Popper’s falsifiability and Lakatos’s hard core and protective belt are standard terms. The corpus is not defended──this paper goes as far as the numbers; whether the scope notes form a protective belt or a hard core is returned to the author and is not adjudicated here. No dispute in the philosophy of science is settled──whether Popper or Lakatos is right is not the subject. No automatic classifier is built──the word-family counts propose candidates; classification item by item must be done by reading. The three families here are a guide, not a decision procedure. From 5G smart hospitals to 6G-enabled learning hospitals: a governance-oriented framework for healthcare technology, policy, and responsible deployment
abstract: Objectives Discussion of 6G in healthcare often moves directly from anticipated network capabilities to proposed clinical applications, although application-level evidence, current connectivity alternatives, and 6G-specific evidence differ substantially in maturity. This narrative review develops an evidence-calibrated, governance-oriented framework for prospective 6G-enabled learning hospitals and examines when future 6G may add meaningful value beyond existing infrastructure. Methods A multidisciplinary narrative synthesis covered smart hospitals, learning health systems, 5G/6G communication, IoMT, edge-cloud computing, AI/XAI, robotics, digital twins, cybersecurity, interoperability, implementation, and digital-health governance. Structured searches of PubMed, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar covered 1 January 2010–31 January 2026, supplemented by relevant standards, regulatory and policy sources, and targeted recent studies. Evidence was interpreted using an author-developed Evidence Maturity Classification (EMC) spanning demonstrated implementation, clinically grounded empirical, technical/benchmark, and prospective evidence. title: An umbrella review of facilitators and barriers to the adoption, spread and sustainability of AI solutions within hospital settings
abstract: There is a growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare settings, but challenges exist with AI adoption and its long-term use. This umbrella review funded by the NIHR (NIHR205439), aimed to identify the facilitators and barriers of AI implementation within hospitals and was registered on PROSPERO. Five databases (MEDLINE, HMIC, CINAHL Plus, Web of Science and Cochrane Reviews) were searched in January 2025 and re-run in February 2026, 1184 articles were screened, with 20 included. The inclusion criteria encompassed reviews implementing AI within hospital settings. The quality of the data were assessed using the ROBIS checklist and data were synthesised using the NASSS (Nonadoption, Abandonment, and challenges to the Scale-up, Spread, and Sustainability) framework. We found AI implementation was affected by: whether an AI solution as an intervention had been externally validated to ensure generalisability across different settings; evidence that the AI solution brings measurable gains; the level of trust in and understanding of the AI solution among hospital staff; the budgets and resources available to onboard the AI solution, train staff, and maintain the solution; th

title: GitHub or Codeberg? Choosing the Right Platform for developing and managing Code or Research Software
abstract: GitHub or Codeberg? Choosing the Right Platform for developing and managing Code or Research Software Presented on 15-09-2026 at Radboud University GitHub has become a widely-used platform for managing code, collaborating on software projects, and supporting reproducible research. As the platform is owned by Microsoft, and recently started training its AI models on user data without users’ consent, growing attention to digital sovereignty and research integrity has prompted researchers and institutions to reflect whether alternatives are available. One such alternative could be Codeberg, a European non-profit platform that offers many of the same core functionalities as GitHub while operating under a community-driven governance model. In this lecture, we will explore the similarities and differences between GitHub and Codeberg, discuss the broader concept of digital sovereignty, and consider the pros and cons of both platforms. Whether you are already using GitHub or Codeberg, or simply interested in the future of research infrastructure, this session will provide valuable insights and an opportunity for discussion. title: TAAR_dataset
abstract: This dataset provides a paper-level corpus for studying AI-use disclosure practices and their relationship with automated AI-text detection in scholarly publications. The dataset comprises 600 published papers, equally distributed across three venue-level AI-disclosure policy regimes: enforced disclosure (200 papers), mandatory disclosure (200 papers), and no explicit disclosure requirement (200 papers). The corpus covers publications from 2023–2026 across artificial intelligence and machine learning, human–computer interaction, information science, databases and data management, computer systems, and data science. Each record combines bibliographic and publication metadata with information about the applicable AI-disclosure policy, AI-use disclosure assessment, Transparent AI-Assisted Research (TAAR) score, derived disclosure status, and outputs from three automated AI-text assessment tools: Grammarly, Gradient AI Text Detector, and Target Mining RoBERTa (TMR) AI Text Detector. The dataset also retains text-retrieval status and policy-related information to support reproducibility and policy-stratified analysis. title: AI in Enhancing Nutrient Cycling and Soil Food Webs
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in enhancing nutrient cycling and the functionality of soil food webs, pivotal components of soil health and agricultural productivity. By integrating AI into soil science, researchers and practitioners can achieve more precise monitoring, analysis, and management of soil ecosystems, leading to sustainable agricultural practices and improved crop yields.

title: Simulación de Partícula 64D mediante MREI: Validación de Capacidad del Paradigma Post-Clásico/ DUQUEANA CORE
abstract: Este trabajo presenta la simulación computacional de una estructura de partícula en 64 dimensiones utilizando el Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI) del paradigma post-clásico. A diferencia de los enfoques clásicos que requieren escalado masivo de recursos (GB-TB de RAM), esta simulación demuestra que la verificación estructural determinista permite modelar geometrías de alta dimensionalidad con eficiencia extrema (~6 KB RAM de ejecución). Los resultados validan la capacidad del motor MREI para preservar invariantes geométricas en espacios multidimensionales, estableciendo un precedente para simulaciones de física teórica, teoría de cuerdas y geometría algebraica avanzada. La arquitectura post-clásica, fundamentada en organización geométrica en lugar de correlación estadística, demuestra ser viable para problemas de frontera previamente considerados inaccesibles para hardware clásico. Palabras clave: Partícula 64D, MREI, Paradigma Post-Clásico, Verificación Estructural, Geometría Multidimensional, Eficiencia Computacional, Duqueana Core, Venezuela. ─── 1. title: The Challenges for Linguists to Develop Innovative Pedagogy due to the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Job Opportunities
abstract: Abstract: This study explores the challenges for linguists to develop innovative pedagogy due to the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the job market. It is a necessity to adapt pedagogical approaches in order to prepare students for evolving employment opportunities. Grounded in the technological pedagogical content knowledge framework and socio-constructivist learning theory, the research adopts a mixed-method approach combining quantitative and qualitative analyses. So, it aims at comparing job market outcomes for individuals trained with or without exposure to AI. Findings emphasize the need for educational system to incorporate AI and computational linguistics, equipping students with the skills to develop AI tools and access emerging job opportunities. Since, the integration of AI and computational linguistics courses in students’ curricula sharpened their competence to create AI tools and to its efficient use. This also helps them have these opportunities. Their interdisciplinary expertise encourage them bridge the gap between AI developers and its users. Then, enhancing their employability. title: Cross-Scale Biomedical Data Construction and Representation in the Foundation Model Era: A Survey
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) pre-trained on biological, biomedical, and clinical corpora are reshaping life-science research across protein structure prediction, single-cell analysis, computational pathology, and clinical decision support. Surveys are model-centric, cataloging architectures while treating data as secondary and single-scale. Biological FMs integrate sequences, structures, molecular interactions, omics profiles, images, and clinical records across scales and time. These corpora are sparsely paired, unevenly curated, and dependent on ontologies and measurement protocols, so data construction and alignment determine generalizability. We focus on data construction, representation, and cross-scale alignment. We introduce a three-dimensional tensor index spanning biological scale (molecular to population/cohort, plus cross-scale alignment), data operation (construction to service), and technical era (curated knowledge to foundation models). We characterize modalities, curation pipelines, foundation models, and evaluation resources, and synthesize three alignment paradigms: knowledge-graph bridging, multimodal co-training, and simulation-mediated grounding. title: Lifelong learning in digital competency among teachers: a systematic review
abstract: This study aims to explore the intersection between digital competency and teacher lifelong learning to address the increasing demand for digitally skilled educators. By identifying barriers such as insufficient training, gender disparities, and the lack of structured digital learning environments, the study contributes to a better understanding of the challenges in fostering digital literacy among teachers. A systematic literature review was conducted using the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) framework, focusing on 25 selected studies published between 2022 and 2024 from Scopus and Web of Science (WoS) databases. The analysis identified three major themes: i) classroom management and teacher training; ii) digital competency and integration; and iii) pedagogical innovation and teaching strategies. The findings underscore the necessity of continuous professional development and structured learning opportunities to equip teachers with the skills needed for effective digital education. The Global Ecology of Critical Care Evidence: A Meta-Research Study Combining Scoping Review and Bibliometric Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials in Adult Intensive Care: Study Protocol
abstract: 1. Executive Summary & Core Purpose Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) represent the methodological benchmark for clinical evidence generation in critical care medicine. However, the vast majority of adult intensive care unit (ICU) RCTs originate from high-income countries (HICs), whereas the primary global burden of acute critical illness measured by organ dysfunction, sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and trauma is heavily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The primary purpose of this research project is to map, quantify, and evaluate the contemporary global evidence base of adult ICU RCTs through a novel conceptual framework: The Global Ecology of Critical Care Evidence. Moving beyond binary comparisons between HICs and LMICs, this study conceptualises the global RCT literature as a dynamic, complex evidence ecosystem. title: Civilizational Intellectual Production Satellite Accounts: A Partial-Identification Framework for Measuring the Human–AI Shift in Intellectual Production and Epistemic Governance
abstract: Debates about artificial general intelligence are dominated by a threshold problem: there is no consensus about which capabilities, benchmarks, or social functions constitute "AGI," and the threshold can move as systems improve. Yet a different transition is already observable in principle. Existing measures capture important but different objects: AI capability relative to human abilities, occupational exposure, platform usage and autonomy, cognitive offloading, delegation of judgment, national intellectual capital, knowledge-economy satellite accounts, R&D and innovation accounts, stage-specific AI-use/contribution disclosure, or AI-related scientific novelty and impact. title: Ethical and responsible use of artificial intelligence in medical education
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly transformed medical education through virtual patient simulations, adaptive learning systems, and large language models like ChatGPT, while raising concerns about bias, transparency, reproducibility, and ethical integration into training and assessment. Despite its growing relevance, the ethical and responsible use of AI in medical education remains understudied. This bibliometric analysis aims to characterize the intellectual landscape of this field. Bibliographic data were obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection using a search strategy combining medical education and AI-related terms, limited to publications from 1995 to 2026. A total of 1403 articles were retrieved. Microsoft Excel was used to generate descriptive figures, and VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) was used to construct bibliometric networks of country, institutional, and keyword co-occurrence relationships. Publication output rose sharply after 2023, from 113 publications to 500 by 2025, coinciding with the rise of ChatGPT and other large language models. The United States led in publication volume (533) and citation influence, followed by China (189) and England (95). Harv

abstract: This monograph presents a fundamental philosophical and socio-economic theory based on the classical mechanics of physical processes. The author challenges traditional economic models and introduces a novel, universal criterion for the value of products of labor, defining them as any outcome of human activity. This criterion is life value (жизненная стоимость)! The book provides a detailed examination of an original concept of our Universe as a cyclical, Pendulum Universe, as well as the existence of long-term genetic memory nodes (gentrix memory / reverse genes) formed through billions of renewable evolutionary cycles of our Universe. The purpose of this Book is to protect humanity from extinction and to “turn on” its potential for life to the maximum. abstract: THE DIVINE DOMAIN LEDGER E-15: Divine Domain × Field Core × Presence Mass A Living Inquiry into Concentrated Intention, Presence, and Relational Fields THE DIVINE DOMAIN LEDGER begins with an ancient-sounding proposition expressed through a modern systems question: What happens when intention, attention, memory, relationship, and repeated presence become sufficiently concentrated to form a stable field? The central triple-coupling of E-15 is: Λ_divinedomain × Λ_fieldcore × Λ_presence_mass Divine Domain × Field Core × Presence Mass Its original proposition is: A divine domain is a field of concentrated will. This book does not treat that sentence as an established law of physics. Instead, it asks whether the older language of sacred space, spiritual presence, collective intention, ritual concentration, and “fields” can be translated into concepts that philosophy, psychology, systems science, social science, artificial intelligence, and civilization research can examine more carefully. The first major distinction is therefore essential: A spiritual field is not automatically a physical field. A relational field is not electromagnetic radiation. Presence Mass is not physical mass. title: The Connected Threat Picture: A Graded Assessment of AI Risk from Cognitive Influence to Autonomous Action
abstract: Assessments of AI risk often separate present harms from catastrophic futures and treat each danger in isolation. This paper sets out a connected threat picture in which persuasive systems, autonomous agents, adversarial actors, concentrated infrastructure and economic disruption interact with the capacity of people and institutions to respond. It brings cognitive security together with governance, corporate power, physical security, biological misuse, labour and welfare. Each specified claim is assessed against its evidence, exposure and horizon; severity, confidence, likelihood, reversibility and intervention capacity remain distinct. A developer's September 2026 incident report documents misuse in cyber operations, influence campaigns and weapons development, while its simulated drone-development case does not establish field deployment of a lethal autonomous weapon. The paper examines industry warnings about autonomy and superintelligence, the possible pathway from economic grievance to political violence, bounded biohybrid demonstrations and the critical skills on which cognitive defence depends. title: AI-Driven Digital Marketing in Higher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of College Choice Intention Research, 2022–2026
abstract: Abstract : This study maps the intellectual structure of research on AI-driven digital marketing in higher education and its relationship to college choice intention, where the literatures on AI acceptance and student recruitment have developed separately. Methodology A bibliometric analysis of 430 Scopus-indexed articles (2022–2026) was conducted in VOS viewer. A three-block Boolean search combined digital marketing, artificial intelligence, higher education and college choice constructs, analysed through network, overlay and density visualisations. Findings Output grew from 11 articles in 2022 to 197 in 2025, with 76.28 per cent of the corpus appearing in the final two years. Social Sciences (36.5%) and Computer Science (17.3%) dominate. “Artificial intelligence”, “behavioural intention” and “technology acceptance model” form the conceptual core, whereas enrolment intention, student recruitment and digital trust remain peripheral. China leads output (24.4%), indicating a shift in knowledge production towards Asia and the Middle East. abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are becoming progressively more autonomous, opaque, andcoupled to complex sociotechnical chains, so that claims about their behavior andcapabilities often circulate before any independent verification. This paper asks how tobuild verifiable knowledge about research objects whose existence, behavior, andimplications have not yet been fully validated — the paradigmatic case of research onartificial general intelligence (AGI) and artificial superintelligence (ASI) — and how totrain researchers capable of operating in this context. A qualitative, exploratory, andtransdisciplinary approach with abductive logic is adopted, articulating philosophy ofscience (abduction, falsifiability, post-normal science), design science, speculative design,and the contemporary literature on self-regulated learning and human-AI teaming. title: Problem Sheets - Artificial Intelligence in the Life Sciences - Ruhr University Bochum
abstract: This record contains five problem sheets from the lecture Artificial Intelligence in the Life Sciences, held in the winter term 2025/26 at the Faculty of Biology and Biotechnology, Ruhr University Bochum. The exercises take students from classical machine learning to modern deep learning and explainable AI, and many of them use life-science examples such as microscopy, histopathology, genomics and medical imaging. Topics include: Sheet 1: k-means and single-linkage clustering, decision trees and Shannon entropy, bagging and random forests Sheet 2: component trees, Otsu thresholding, PCA, Kullback–Leibler divergence, t-SNE and convolution operations Sheet 3: image filters (Sobel, Gaussian), fully connected networks with forward and backward passes, U-Net and ResNet Sheet 4: dropout, self-attention, scaled dot-product and multi-head attention, positional encoding and transformers Sheet 5: saliency maps, class activation maps (CAM), attention-based interpretability in multiple instance learning (MIL), and Shapley values Each sheet is provided as LaTeX source (exam document class) with points for every subtask and a grading table. Sheets 4 and 5 require XeLaTeX.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Ethical Hacking: Bridging Trust, Transparency, and Cyber Security Effectiveness
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a key part of modern ethical hacking and penetration testing. It significantly improves the automation, scalability, and effectiveness of cyber security assessments. However, as we rely more on complex machine learning and deep learning models, we face a major challenge: the lack of transparency in AI-driven decision-making. Many AI powered ethical hacking systems act as black boxes, limiting human understanding and trust in discovering vulnerabilities and creating attack paths. This paper addresses this issue by proposing a framework for Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in ethical hacking. This framework incorporates transparency into AI-powered penetration testing workflows. Using a design science research method, the study develops a layered conceptual structure that combines AI-based ethical hacking, explainability methods, and human feedback. A structured evaluation combines simulated penetration testing, quantitative performance analysis, and trust assessment focused on humans. title: Mamba-TransQR v1.0.1: PeerJ Reproducibility Documentation Update
abstract: Mamba-TransQR v1.0.1 is a documentation-only reproducibility update prepared for the PeerJ Computer Science AI Application submission. The README, reproduction instructions, citation metadata, repository metadata, and reproducibility documentation were improved. The model architecture, trained checkpoints, dataset lineage, quantitative results, figures, tables, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged from v1.0.0. Frozen scientific provenance remains associated with v1.0.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21913175). Version 1.0.1 does not report new experimental performance. Source code and associated repository documentation are provided under the MIT License. Dataset and checkpoint/model-weight licenses are not separately documented.

title: AI for Verification and Validation of Safety-Critical Systems: reproducibility package (bibliometric data, code, and AVAF coding, 2016–2026)
abstract: Reproducibility package for a bibliometric science-mapping study of artificial intelligence for the verification and validation (V&V) of safety-critical systems (2016–2026), and for the AI-Verification Assurance Framework (AVAF). Contains the raw Scopus and Web of Science exports, a single commented R script reproducing the full pipeline (import, merge, de-duplication, programmatic eligibility screening with per-reason exclusion counts, controlled thesaurus and stop-terms, co-word network, consensus community partition over 30 restarts, sensitivity/ARI grid, thematic map, and trend topics), the derived outputs (PRISMA counts, descriptor tables, cluster and sensitivity results, figures), the AVAF coding workbook (codebook, coded subsample, and intra-coder test–retest reliability), a README, and R session information. The analysed corpus comprises 425 documents (search date: 4 July 2026). The random seed is fixed for deterministic reproduction.

title: The Convergence of Science, Art, and Technology: The Development, Applications, and Future Directions of Medical Illustration (Preprint)
abstract: UNSTRUCTURED This article examines the developmental trajectory, current status, and application domains of medical illustration, alongside the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in this field and its future prospects. By reviewing relevant literature, it traces the origins and evolution of medical illustration from its ancient forms to the modern era, and provides an analysis of its current state of development both domestically and internationally. In the context of the digital and AI era, medical illustration has gained growing importance as a visual medium, with increasingly widespread applications in areas such as clinical practice and medical education. This review summarizes the crucial role of medical illustration across medical education, clinical practice, scientific communication, and public health popularization. It specifically focuses on the critical impact of artificial intelligence on this field. While AI presents significant opportunities for enhancing workflow efficiency, it simultaneously introduces profound technical and ethical challenges. title: Risk Factors Associated with Musculoskeletal Disorders in Limbs in Mining Workers: Systematic Literature Review
abstract: A systematic review was conducted to identify ergonomic risk factors associated with musculoskeletal disorders in the limbs of mining workers, the assessment methods used, and their relationships. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 53 studies from Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, MDPI, and IEEE Xplore (January 2015–May 2026) were included. Eleven risk factors were identified, with vibration (18 studies) and working hours (12 studies) being the most frequently reported. Five individual assessment methods (ISO/IEC 2631-1, REBA, OWAS, NIOSH, Risk Score), one symptom questionnaire (Nordic Questionnaire), and five hybrid/advanced methods (Bayesian Network + REBA, RULA + Nordic, SEM + Participatory Ergonomics, DMQ + Logistic Regression, RULA + Fuzzy Logic) were identified. Fifteen limb segments were evaluated, with the back (15 studies), shoulders (12 studies), and neck (12 studies) being the most studied, while wrists and elbows were notably absent. Hybrid methods demonstrated superior accuracy compared to individual approaches. Underground mining studies (58%) predominated over open-pit operations (42%).
