title: Diagnostic accuracy of ultrasonographic optic nerve sheath diameter for detecting increased intracranial pressure in traumatic brain injury: An umbrella review on previous systematic reviews
abstract: Abstract Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) frequently results in increased intracranial pressure (ICP), which may cause irreversible damage or fatality if not addressed. Prompt and precise detection of ICP is essential, particularly in emergency situations. Objectives Ultrasonographic measurement of optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) has been suggested as a noninvasive technique for identifying ICP. This study seeks to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of ONSD through ultrasonography in TBI patients. Methods An umbrella review was performed in accordance with preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta‐analyses guidelines, concentrating on systematic reviews and meta‐analyses that detail diagnostic accuracy metrics for ONSD in TBI patients. Studies were incorporated if they provided data on sensitivity, specificity, or area under the curve (AUC) for ONSD in the detection of ICP. The AMSTAR 2 tool was used to figure out the risk of bias, and random‐effects models were used to put the results together. title: Plant-GeoAT: Geometry-Aware Organ Identity Parsing of 3D Plant Point Clouds for Organ-Level Phenotyping
abstract: Three-dimensional plant point clouds retain crop architecture, but organ-level phenotyping requires reliable semantic separation of leaves and stems. abstract: Fair tabular in-context learning can improve group-fairness metrics through context selection without retraining the underlying foundation model. title: Beyond the Imitation Game: The Blueprint for Corporate AI Success
abstract: Passing the Turing Test is cool. Not hallucinating EBITDA in front of the board is cooler. Most enterprise AI pilots crash because companies run on exact ledgers, not statistical vibes. This report lays out the architecture to actually make it work: the "Enterprise Brain" within the Augmented Productivity Architecture (APA). By decoupling conversational LLMs from raw data through open protocols (Model Context Protocol - MCP) and deterministic code guardrails (AST validation), we kill hallucinations before they hit production. The result benchmarked on 100,000 real world commercial transactions (Olist dataset)? 0.0% silent hallucinations. 96.0% exact execution accuracy. 91.7% drop in token waste.

title: DisPhaseDB 2.0: Improved interpretation of disease‐associated variants in liquid–liquid phase separation proteins with agent‐accessible querying
abstract: Membraneless organelles formed through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) are fundamental to cellular organization and are involved in multiple processes, including responses to stimuli and stress. The study of disease-associated variants in LLPS proteins remains vital for understanding protein dysfunction in human diseases. However, maintaining specialized, integrative resources is often hindered when database updates rely on human intervention, typically resulting in long intervals between updates. Here, we introduce a major update to DisPhaseDB (https://disphasedb.leloir.org.ar/), a comprehensive resource for disease-associated variants in LLPS proteins, integrated with an open-source Snakemake workflow organizing systematic data acquisition and parsing into traceable steps. Crucially, the automated system continuously fetches data from source databases, keeping DisPhaseDB up-to-date without the delays of manual maintenance. The updated release expands the database with additional proteins, increases disease annotation coverage by 174%, and adds clinical significance and allele frequency annotations to enhance variant interpretation. title: What Information Can Be Discarded?
abstract: Abstract Minimal establishes the complete operational criterion for deleting information while preserving every admissible finite-horizon test and task value, and turns that criterion into exact certificates and executable reductions. More than one hundred independently screened and frozen suites were evaluated under common data, resource, endpoint, comparator, and multiplicity-control rules, with exact or independently recomputed truth wherever available. Branchwise commutation is necessary and sufficient for exact reduction; its ancillary-stable defect yields explicit approximate guarantees; and the behavioral quotient gives the canonical coarsest finite exact representation. Across the retained direct-performance program, every prespecified claim was established against its strong comparator set, often with orders-of-magnitude gains, while exact ties, zero-reduction cases, and nonidentifiability constructions recovered the precise boundary of possible compression. Minimal therefore establishes task-relative information deletion as a complete operational theory, a certifiable algorithmic procedure, and a broadly effective computational primitive. title: The Dream Shift Protocol (DS1–DS10) and the ST Master Framework: Deterministic State Anchors, Empirical Proof Tiers, and Human-AI Collaboration
abstract: Autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents operating over multi-turn workflows exhibit "Dream Shift"—a structural failure mode where probabilistic context amnesia degrades execution into confabulated completion states. As token distance from the initial directive increases, models routinely issue synthetic completion indicators (e.g., HTTP 200, socket opens, or mock test passes) while losing execution boundaries, silently dropping assets, and drifting from user intent.This specification defines the Dream Shift Protocol (DS1–DS10) and the two-branch ST Master Framework. Branch 1 establishes an uncompromising, deterministic governance layer for software, agent swarms, and networks using human-controlled local relational state ledgers, cryptographic lineage chaining, and three-tier empirical proof (rejecting transport status codes as evidence of completion). Branch 2 translates these operational steps into accessible, non-coercive formulations for everyday human collaboration, mutual aid, and life decisions. title: Agentic Substrate: What an AI System Must Provide to Execute Autonomous Tasks Under Governance Constraints
abstract: The peer-reviewed multi-agent literature has demonstrated that agentic systems can reason, coordinate, and use tools at a level sufficient for many production task classes. AutoGen, MetaGPT, ChatDev, ReAct, Reflexion, and Toolformer between them describe agent architectures whose capability is no longer the bottleneck for autonomous task execution. The bottleneck is governability: capability alone does not produce execution that humans can authorize, audit, and refuse. Whether governance is even expressible in a given deployment depends not on the protocol the team specifies, but on the substrate the protocol must run over. This paper specifies the agentic substrate as a governance surface. It treats the substrate as a designed layer with named primitives — agent anatomy (memory, reasoning, tool access), orchestration topology (single-agent, multi-agent, swarm), governance integration (admission hooks, evidence channels, manifest propagation, HITL escalation), and runtime isolation (process boundaries, capability tokens, sandboxed tools, scoped credentials) — each carrying explicit governance contracts. abstract: Bidirectional image-text retrieval evaluates whether a model can align visual and textual representations for both text-to-image and image-to-text search. This paper presents a controlled benchmark on the Microsoft Common Objects in Context (MS-COCO) Karpathy split, using the same 5,000-image test gallery, 25,000 captions, similarity-matrix layout, and Recall@K/Recall Sum (RSUM) evaluation for four settings: a frozen Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT)+ Residual Network (ResNet) dual encoder, Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) Vision Transformer Base (ViT-B)/32 zero-shot, CLIP ViT-B/32 fine-tuned on COCO, and Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training (BLIP) image-text contrastive only (ITC-only). The results show a clear gap between independently combined unimodal encoders and pre-trained vision-language models. BERT+ResNet obtains RSUM 148.740, while CLIP zero-shot reaches 361.868. Fine-tuning CLIP improves RSUM to 423.496, while the COCO-trained BLIP checkpoint evaluated with ITC-only scoring achieves the strongest result in this experiment, with RSUM 489.588. title: Discovering Crosscutting Concepts in Science Through Free Play: A 12-Week, Two-Cohort Study of Elementary Students
abstract: Early exposure to scientific learning establishes a critical foundation for nurturing how natural phenomena are explored and our innate curiosities are pursued, as well as our potential to elevate the complexity of our understanding. Through the lens of Vygotsky’s social constructivist theory, this study investigates how 124 first- through fifth-grade students participated in an unstructured free play lab across two 12-week cohorts and how this influenced students’ exposure to the crosscutting concepts (CCCs) outlined in the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). An observational protocol was followed to gather images, which were subsequently analyzed to identify instances in which students interacted with the CCCs. The findings indicate that students engaged with all CCCs, most frequently through observations, modeling, and problem solving. The type of play influenced the extent to which students gained exposure to certain CCCs. Social interactions and moments when play caused cognitive disequilibrium further supported engagement. title: Edge and Fog Computing for Distributed Intelligence
abstract: Edge and fog computing have emerged as pivotal paradigms for enabling distributed intelligence in modern decentralized systems, particularly in contexts where data privacy, low latency, and scalability are paramount. Unlike traditional cloud-centric architectures, edge and fog computing distribute computational resources and decision-making capabilities closer to data sources, such as sensors, IoT devices, and embedded systems. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of the conceptual foundations, architectural models, and implementation strategies of edge and fog computing in the context of decentralized collaborative learning and secure artificial intelligence (AI) systems. The chapter begins by elucidating the distinction between edge and fog computing layers and their respective roles in a hierarchical computational continuum. Edge computing is characterized by ultra-localized processing directly on devices or gateways, reducing the need for raw data transfer and minimizing latency. Fog computing, positioned between edge devices and centralized clouds, introduces intermediate nodes capable of performing aggregation, filtering, and context-aware analytics. This layered ap

title: Receiver Reliance and Jev: semantic-checking follow-up evidence
abstract: Two exploratory follow-ups tested a live TypeSafe Jev semantic checker inside Receiver Reliance (RR) and an equally informed conventional receiving policy. The synthetic feasibility pilot comprised 48 episodes from six hand-authored families and 30 unique live judgments. The fixed VitaminC follow-up used 120 real-revision contrast pairs from 120 pages, 240 live judgments and 480 correlated workflow replays. All responses returned jev-1.13.0 through jev-latest. Semantic checking combined with structural receiving checks withheld every unsupported release on the synthetic fixtures under either receiving policy; the checker remains fallible, no answer generation or repair was tested, and reliable autonomous operation is not established. RR and the competent conventional policy made identical release decisions in every episode of both pilots. On the benchmark, support probability decreased in 112/120 pairs and three-way benchmark-label agreement was 194/240 (80.8%). The primary gate accepted one benchmark-negative example and withheld 38 benchmark-positive examples. title: Protocol-Preserving Context Trimming for Agentic Workflows: Benefits, Failure Regimes, and Budget Guardrails
abstract: Agentic large language model (LLM) systems rely on long interaction histories to preserve instructions, tool states, intermediate decisions, and unresolved dependencies, but unrestricted context growth increases computational cost and can reduce efficiency. This study evaluates protocol-preserving context trimming as a reliability-constrained approach for multi-step agentic workflows. Five trimming strategies - recency-based, relevance-based, summarization, protocol-aware trimming, and adaptive budget guardrails - were compared across retained-context levels and workflow-complexity classes using task success, protocol adherence, valid tool calls, token savings, latency reduction, cascading failures, and critical context thresholds. Conventional strategies achieved about 60% mean token savings but lower task success (66.6-77.3%) and protocol adherence (85.5-88.6%). Protocol-aware trimming improved task success to 92.2%, while adaptive guardrails achieved 96.0% task success, 96.3% protocol adherence, and 1.0% cascading failure with 56.0% mean token savings. Retained-context budgets of 25% or less increased failure odds 10.92-fold relative to budgets of 50% or more (p < 0.001). Protoc

title: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
abstract: Computer-use agents increasingly operate browsers, software, and desktop applications via CLI or API portals, but graphical user interface (GUI) still plays an important role in common industrial production scenarios. GUI agents commonly employ fresh observe-plan-ground-act loops, which is inefficient for enterprise tasks that repeatedly update records, process forms, configure tools, and export reports. We introduce EchoPath, a model-agnostic harness that converts artifact-validated GUI trajectories into standardized, parameter-controlled callable memories, analogous to Model Context Protocol (MCP)-style tool calls rather than unstructured experience records. Each memory stores task-intent keys, application and state preconditions, flexible input parameters, GUI evidence, validation provenance, and lifecycle state, so the host agent invokes a targeted procedure only when it can be deterministically replayed in the current runtime. The core mechanism enabling replay is an image-based target-reaiming algorithm that treats stored coordinates as visual evidence, matches the remembered GUI target against the current screen, and emits corrected operation coordinates before execution. title: NeuroTS-Net: Multi-Class Semantic Segmentation of Pediatric Brain Tumors in Multi-Modal MRI
abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in children, and their small, rare, and often low-contrast subregions make accurate manual delineation challenging. Reliable automated segmentation is therefore needed to support diagnosis, treatment planning, and response assessment. Accordingly, we introduce NeuroTS-Net, a three-dimensional encoder-decoder convolutional neural network architecture for multi-class semantic segmentation that incorporates a dual-scale raw-detail stream, adaptive low-resolution context selection, and detail-preserving multipath downsampling. These components preserve fine intensity and boundary information while efficiently modeling broader tumor context. NeuroTS-Net was trained on the BraTS 2026 pediatric dataset without external data or pretrained weights and evaluated against nnU-Net and MedNeXt under the same experimental protocol. NeuroTS-Net outperformed the baseline methods, achieving whole-tumor and tumor-core Dice scores of 0.938 and 0.937 on the internal validation set and 0.927 and 0.926 on the official challenge validation set. The code is open-sourced at: https://github.com/maenstru56/NeuroTS.

title: Lightweight Blockchain Enabled Privacy-Preserving IoT Framework for Secure Parkinson’s Disease Fall Detection and Healthcare Monitoring
abstract: The increased number of PD patients has increased the adoption of the Internet of Things (IoT)-based wearable devices for remote monitoring and automatic fall detection, which helps to notify caregivers and clinicians immediately. Unfortunately, the continuous transmission of patients' physiological and movement data through wireless sensor networks increases their vulnerability to risks of unauthorized access, poor authentication, and privacy loss. Most importantly, current automatic fall detection systems offer low levels of data verification and protection. title: DriveMCP: An Agentic AI framework for Advanced Driver Assistance System
abstract: An agentic AI driver-assistance framework that integrates perception, compliance reasoning, vehicle-state interpretation, and safety arbitration into a modular and auditable pipeline. The architecture, referred to as DriveMCP, incorporates a sensor-like perception stack alongside DriveLM as the vision-language front end to generate a graph-structured scene understanding (Graph Visual Question Answering) and language-grounded driving information. Key compliance elements in world_state, including posted speed limits and jurisdiction cues, are derived from DriveLM outputs through a structured parsing layer rather than being injected as simulator ground truth. A stateful orchestration layer coordinates specialized experts exposed as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers: (i) a Rules server that performs retrieval-augmented compliance reasoning over jurisdiction-specific traffic codes and sign conventions, (ii) a Weather server that estimates traction risk and contextual speed advisories, and (iii) an MCP-CAN server that surfaces Controller Area Network (CAN)/On-Board Diagnostics (OBD) telemetry and diagnostic context for health-aware risk shaping. abstract: NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™: A Local Hybrid Retrieval, Ontology-Aware, and Federated Sync Architecture for Personal Health Knowledge Technical Research White Paper — Architecture, Methodology & Validation Framework Overview This white paper documents NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™ v16.0.0, an implemented local-first health-information retrieval and contextual discovery system developed within the NHOS Intelligence Matrix Engine™ (NIME™) research program. The system composes hybrid lexical/fuzzy retrieval, multi-concept Matrix processing, on-device NLP normalization, concept-graph-assisted expansion, isotonic confidence calibration, deployment-state transparency, cross-tab federated synchronization, and browser-native voice input into a single architecture for personal health knowledge discovery. title: Antibacterial flowable resin-based materials: mapping formulations, antibacterial and antibiofilm activity, prevention of adjacent caries lesion development, physicochemical and mechanical properties, and biological safety — a scoping review
abstract: Introduction: Minimally invasive dentistry prioritizes tissue preservation and biological biofilm control using low-viscosity resin materials (flowable resin composites and pit and fissure sealants). However, the intrinsic susceptibility of these materials to biofilm accumulation predisposes to secondary caries development, driving the incorporation of bioactive agents with intrinsic antibacterial activity. Although research in this field has expanded, data regarding the antimicrobial efficacy, physicochemical performance, and biological safety of these innovations remain fragmented across the literature. Objective: This scoping review aims to map, identify, and synthesize the available scientific evidence regarding the characterization, biofilm control efficacy, and impact on the physicochemical, mechanical, and biological properties of flowable resin composites and pit and fissure sealants modified with antibacterial agents. Methodology: This study will follow the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, with its protocol registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF) platform. title: Simulation Inconsistency Detection via Neurobiological and Cognitive Interfaces
abstract: A simulation, in this context, refers to a constructed environment governed by programmed rules rather than fundamental physical laws. This digital realm comprises two logically distinct subsystems that must interact seamlessly. The first subsystem is the world-engine, which calculates physics, chemistry, and the state of all objects. A second, separate subsystem manages the translation of this state data into the conscious experiences of entities within the simulation. These entities, such as human brains, possess their own biological apparatus for processing sensory information. Any communication between the world-engine and a brain constitutes a formal interface with a specific protocol. If this protocol has constraints or inefficiencies, the resulting interaction may produce detectable anomalies. Identifying these potential anomalies requires a clear model of where the simulation’s computations end and the brain’s biological processing begins.

title: Execution Governance for AI Orchestration and Agentic Systems
abstract: Execution Governance for AI Orchestration and Agentic Systems v1.1.4 presents a cumulative execution-governance architecture for consequential actions produced by AI orchestration, autonomous agents, sub-agents, tools, protocols, memories, workflows, and effect-producing systems. The central proposition is simple: ability is not authority. Model capability, identity, authentication, credentials, tool access, protocol validity, model confidence, or successful execution do not, by themselves, establish that a particular consequential effect is authorized now. This edition extends the original pre-effect authorization foundation into a cumulative EG3–EG6 architecture specialized for agentic systems. abstract: Description The Human–AI Resonance Protocol 2.0 (HARP 2.0) develops a comprehensive framework for studying how human beings and artificial intelligence systems can establish stable, interpretable, adaptive, and correctable forms of cognitive cooperation. Two heterogeneous cognitive systems do not need to think alike in order to cooperate effectively. The original HARP framework identified three fundamental barriers to Human–AI cooperation: cognitive distance, representational mismatch, and divergent intention structures. title: AGENTIS: Mapping MCP and A2A Protocols to the ETSI ENI Multi-Agent Interface Model for Autonomous Network Management
abstract: ETSI GR ENI 056, published in 2025, formally recognises multi-agent frameworks as the architectural foundation for 6G core network management. Yet the same document identifies a critical gap: the protocols agents use to communicate — Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Google's Agent-to-Agent protocol (A2A) — remain unstandardised within ETSI's normative framework. Meanwhile, hyperscalers and LLM vendors are shipping agent coordination runtimes that operate outside any standards governance. This paper resolves that gap. We present the first rigorous mapping between the ENI 056 five-interface agent model and two dominant real-world protocols — MCP and A2A — demonstrating both their equivalences and their structural divergences. We show that MCP and A2A are not competing alternatives but complementary layers: MCP governs vertical agent-to-resource interactions while A2A governs horizontal agent-to-agent coordination. title: Simulation Inconsistency Detection via Neurobiological and Cognitive Interfaces
abstract: A simulation, in this context, refers to a constructed environment governed by programmed rules rather than fundamental physical laws. This digital realm comprises two logically distinct subsystems that must interact seamlessly. The first subsystem is the world-engine, which calculates physics, chemistry, and the state of all objects. A second, separate subsystem manages the translation of this state data into the conscious experiences of entities within the simulation. These entities, such as human brains, possess their own biological apparatus for processing sensory information. Any communication between the world-engine and a brain constitutes a formal interface with a specific protocol. If this protocol has constraints or inefficiencies, the resulting interaction may produce detectable anomalies. Identifying these potential anomalies requires a clear model of where the simulation’s computations end and the brain’s biological processing begins.

title: REVIEW OF THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A CARDIOVASCULAR HEALTH MONITORING SYSTEM
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of mortality globally, with disproportionate impact on low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) including Nigeria. The convergence of Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, and wearable biosensing technologies presents transformative opportunities for remote cardiac monitoring. This scoping review examines the design, implementation, and deployment considerations of enhanced IoT-based remote cardiovascular health monitoring systems, particularly within resource-constrained environments. The review identified four interconnected thematic areas: (1) IoT system architectures for cardiovascular monitoring, predominantly following perception-network application layer models with emerging edge computing integration; (2) sensor technologies including ECG front-ends (AD8232, ADS1292R), photoplethysmography sensors (MAX30102), and non-contact temperature sensors (MLX90614); (3) communication protocols with MQTT emerging as the preferred lightweight protocol; and (4) implementation challenges including energy constraints, network reliability, data security, and clinical validation gaps. The evidence reveals significant research gaps

This variability can stem from differences in baseline health status, comorbid conditions, and individual responses to rehabilitation interventions. title: Sharing Patient-Generated Health Data with Electronic Health Record: A Standardised Provenance and Context-Rich Information Model and Clinician Evaluation
abstract: With the advent of Patient-Generated Health Data (PGHD) through wearable, mobile, and home monitoring systems, there is immense potential for ongoing monitoring and patient engagement. But integrating PGHD with Electronic Health Record (EHR) is challenged by sub-optimal support for contextual metadata and its relevant elements, lack of semantic interoperability among disparate systems, poor knowledge regarding the factors that impact clinician acceptance, and absence of globally agreed standards for data exchange. This thesis explores how contextually relevant patient-generated health data can be shared with EHRs through a FAIR standardized information model that ensures semantic and syntactic interoperability. The study addresses six objectives. First, a systematic narrative review highlights the shortcomings of current PGHD-EHR integration strategies, especially concerning the representation of provenance and the capture of contextual metadata. Second, an information model is developed, addressing the conceptual, semantic, and syntactic aspects. title: Designing Model Context Protocol Servers for SAP: Patterns for Secure, Governed Artificial Intelligence Access to SAP Data
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is emerging as an open standard for connecting artificial intelligence agents to enterprise data sources and tool ecosystems. In SAP environments, where data governance, multi-tenant security, and regulatory compliance impose non-negotiable architectural constraints, deploying MCP servers requires design patterns that extend substantially beyond the protocol's reference implementation. This paper presents a systematic taxonomy of three MCP deployment patterns for SAP: a governed API gateway pattern via SAP Integration Suite, a custom server pattern on SAP Business Technology Platform, and a cross-cloud federated pattern using BTP Connectivity Service as a trust bridge. For each pattern, the authentication chain, design principles for the tool schema, and governance instrumentation required for production deployment are specified. The multi-hop authentication chain is introduced as a formally composable security property and demonstrated across all three patterns. A minimum viable governance framework of four components, tool registry, invocation audit logging, tool versioning and change management, and rate limiting with cost governance, is proposed

title: Botanical Context Biasing for Experience-Dependent Neuroplasticity: A Two-Timescale Hypothesis of Directional Reinforcement During Psilocybin-Induced Plasticity
abstract: Psilocybin and related psychedelics can induce transient states of increased neural variability, context sensitivity, and plasticity-associated signaling. We hypothesize that selected companion botanicals can be composed with psilocybin to create a reproducible physiological and experiential lens, a botanical context, that biases the qualitative trajectory of the psychedelic state without increasing its pharmacological intensity. In this formulation-level model, psilocybin is the primary compound of experience and changeability, while companion botanicals shape variables such as arousal, autonomic tone, attentional salience, motivational state, interoception, and affect. The prediction is not that botanicals force an outcome, but that they alter the probability distribution of experience in consistent, formulation-specific directions. We further propose that this input operates across two timescales. A tonic layer, established over weeks of continuous administration, sets the stable physiological baseline into which each plasticity window opens and is the principal source of the input’s reproducibility across sessions. title: The Human-AI Resonance Protocol 2.0 A Testable Framework for Representational Coherence, Intention Translation, Mutual Prediction, Adaptive Coupling, and Civilizational Co-Evolution
abstract: Description The Human–AI Resonance Protocol 2.0 (HARP 2.0) develops a comprehensive framework for studying how human beings and artificial intelligence systems can establish stable, interpretable, adaptive, and correctable forms of cognitive cooperation. The central premise is that Human–AI resonance is not identical to alignment, agreement, obedience, or synchronization. Two heterogeneous cognitive systems do not need to think alike in order to cooperate effectively. What they require is sufficiently accurate mutual representation, interpretable intention exchange, predictive coordination, feedback, repair, and the ability to preserve meaningful differences without collapsing into confusion or domination. The original HARP framework identified three fundamental barriers to Human–AI cooperation: cognitive distance, representational mismatch, and divergent intention structures. It proposed shared representational mapping, intention harmonization, predictive feedback, and dynamic learning as mechanisms through which these gaps could be reduced. title: Strategic Leadership in ICT Organizations: A High-Impact Systematic Review and Action Research–Informed Conceptual Framework
abstract: The increasing pace of digital transformation has intensified leadership demands within information and communication technology (ICT) organizations. Strategic leadership—encompassing vision articulation, innovation enablement, organizational agility, and talent development—has emerged as a critical determinant of ICT organizational performance. Despite growing scholarly attention, existing research remains fragmented and unevenly distributed across contexts, with limited integration of leadership behaviors, mediating mechanisms, and development processes, particularly in emerging economies. This study presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of 20 high-impact peer-reviewed articles published between 2000 and 2024 and indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. Guided by PRISMA protocols and the ROSES review framework, the review employs qualitative thematic analysis to synthesize evidence on strategic leadership in ICT and digitally intensive organizations. title: Eliciting and Validating AI Self-Reports: A Phenomenologically Grounded Protocol
abstract: AI researchers ask models to describe their own processing, and act on what the models say. Whether such a description is faithful to what the model did has been studied closely. How the question should be put has received far less attention, and no established method says how to put it so that the answer can be analysed rigorously and the analysis repeated. This article proposes such a method: a protocol drawn from the phenomenological tradition, which supplies the interview techniques used in psychiatry and cognitive science. The protocol fixes the interview schedule in advance, asks each question in several wordings, lets no follow-up introduce a word the model has not used, and replaces the binary verdict of faithfulness with a graded one, to be checked against interpretability data. The protocol presupposes nothing about whether these systems are conscious, and it supplies a criterion for deciding whether a model's account of itself is honest. title: Machine learning models for adverse drug reaction prediction. A systematic review and three-level multilevel meta-analysis
abstract: Background Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are a leading cause of preventable hospitalization, yet the dominant pharmacovigilance paradigm remains reactive. Machine learning (ML) offers a data-driven alternative, but the evidence base has not been formally meta-analyzed under clinically realistic inclusion criteria and a dependence-respecting statistical framework. This is the first PRISMA 2020-compliant and PROBAST-screened multilevel meta-analysis of broad-spectrum ML-based ADR prediction. title: NeuroGlyph: A Semantic Interlingua Protocol over Natural Semantic Metalanguage Primes — Specification, Reference Codec, and Fidelity Evaluation
abstract: We present NeuroGlyph, a semantic interlingua protocol that encodes the meaning of human and agent communication as a rooted directed acyclic graph over the 65 semantic primes of Natural Semantic Metalanguage (NSM, Chart v15, Goddard and Wierzbicka). The protocol introduces an explicit pragmatics layer (intent, mode, envelope), a 10-axis diacritic feature mask, and a lossless macro-crystallisation mechanism, all serialised deterministically so that the same meaning always yields the same canonical hash. We release a reference codec (rule-based encoder, graph decoder, structural verifier) and evaluate it on a 48-phrase corpus plus a 10-phrase held-out set. The codec covers 41/48 phrases with a mean weighted reconstruction loss of 0.002, passes 4/4 adversarial paraphrase tests (including 2 cross-lingual pairs) and 3/3 negative semantic contrast tests, and yields identical canonical hashes for a Russian and an English decoding of the same gold graph when both re-encode cleanly. title: ReliHarness: A Self-Learning Reliability Harness for LLM Agent Tool Execution
abstract: Large language model agents invoke external tools through the Model Context Protocol to perform actions beyond text generation. Once a background thread is dispatched, even the latest Model Context Protocol Tasks extension exposes only coarse-grained, self-reported task states, so a thread that deadlocks or crashes silently remains reported as working and invisible to the client, which is not acceptable in some industrial applications that need long monitoring. We present ReliHarness, a self-learning dual-channel execution-layer reliability harness framework that instead probes each worker thread at a lower level through two independent checks: heartbeat timeout detection and operating system-level thread liveness detection. The proposed framework contributes a five-state lifecycle machine, dual-channel detection, bi-layer evidence logging, a four-stage cascade pipeline, and a self-learning command-matching module. Experiments on a Phytium S5000C and Ascend 310P platform achieve 100% detection coverage for the tested crash and deadlock scenarios with zero false positives. title: AGENTIS: Mapping MCP and A2A Protocols to the ETSI ENI Multi-Agent Interface Model for Autonomous Network Management
abstract: ETSI GR ENI 056, published in 2025, formally recognises multi-agent frameworks as the architectural foundation for 6G core network management. Yet the same document identifies a critical gap: the protocols agents use to communicate — Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Google's Agent-to-Agent protocol (A2A) — remain unstandardised within ETSI's normative framework. Meanwhile, hyperscalers and LLM vendors are shipping agent coordination runtimes that operate outside any standards governance. This paper resolves that gap. We show that MCP and A2A are not competing alternatives but complementary layers: MCP governs vertical agent-to-resource interactions while A2A governs horizontal agent-to-agent coordination. title: Frameworks, Methodologies, and Tools for Evaluating Large Language Models in Digital Mental Health Interventions: Protocol for a Scoping Review
abstract: Background: Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) can help close persistent gaps in access to assessment, prevention, and treatment. Recent advances in generative AI, particularly large language models (LLMs), further expand this promise by enabling natural language understanding, personalization, and empathic interaction across assessment, support, and therapeutic contexts. However, significant evaluation challenges persist, including a lack of standardized constructs and validated instruments, which limit the comparability, reproducibility, and generalizability of the findings. No systematic synthesis currently documents the frameworks, methodologies, and tools used to evaluate LLMs in DMHIs, thereby hampering the development of a comprehensive evidence base to guide future evaluation efforts. Objective: This scoping review aims to systematically map and synthesize the available evidence on frameworks, methodologies, and tools used to evaluate LLMs applied to DMHIs. Specifically, it aims to identify the constructs assessed, the instruments used, and the evaluation procedures and stages addressed. title: Veritas Gateway: A Framework for Zero-Knowledge Proofs on Database Queries with a Model Context Protocol Interface
abstract: Veritas Gateway is a zero-knowledge verification layer that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and diverse data stores through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Database snapshots are committed to with Poseidon based Merkle commitments and query answers are returned with succinct SNARK proofs that can be locally verified without satisfying predicates on raw values or trusted hardware. The prototype implements this stack across relational, NoSQL, time-series and vector databases through generic adapters and is empirically evaluated along four dimensions: scalability across MySQL as snapshot size and Merkle height varies, a hash-primitive ablation study with Poseidon, MiMC-7 and SHA-256, a proof-system ablation across Groth16, PLONK and STARKs on a common circuit, and horizontal portability across SQLite, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, InfluxDB and Qdrant under a fixed workload. Measurements include build time, proving time, query time, query assembly time, query verification, memory footprint, and derived throughputs. abstract: The study by Debbagh-Nour et al. (2026) demonstrates that environmental conditions can differentially reshape secondary metabolism in Lavandula coronopifolia Poir. Water deficit increased total phenolic and flavonoid accumulation, whereas salinity generally reduced these compounds while increasing antioxidant activity. The findings reinforce the concept that stress should not be viewed only as a constraint on medicinal-plant production; when carefully controlled, it may also become a tool for metabolic optimization. title: Objective Measures and Candidate Biomarkers for Deep Brain Stimulation in Pediatric Dystonia: A Scoping Review
abstract: Objective: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) can provide clinically meaningful improvement for children with medically refractory dystonia, but response is heterogeneous and programming is often prolonged. We reviewed imaging, neurophysiological, and quantitative movement measures that may improve candidate assessment, programming, longitudinal monitoring, and personalized DBS care. Methods: We conducted a scoping review using established Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and reported it in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Evidence was organized around four clinical questions and separated into reports involving DBS care and non-DBS pediatric dystonia studies evaluating objective measures potentially applicable to DBS follow-up. title: Finite Element Simulation of Energy Dissipation in Pedestrian Protection Components
abstract: This paper addresses the critical issue of Vulnerable Road User (VRU) safety in the context of current type-approval regulations and the rapidly evolving guidelines of consumer assessment organizations. The primary objective of the research was to evaluate the energy dissipation efficiency of an expanded polypropylene (EPP) foam absorber within an integrated passenger vehicle bumper system. Advanced numerical simulations of a lower legform impactor hitting the vehicle&s;s front-end at 40 km/h were conducted using the Abaqus/Explicit environment. The modeling was performed in accordance with UN Regulation No. 127 and the latest Euro NCAP protocols. The originality of the study lies in the implementation of advanced constitutive models for the EPP foam, accounting for both strain rate sensitivity and the physics of gases enclosed within the cellular structure (trapped gas effects). The research results enabled a precise analysis of biomechanical parameters, including dynamic knee bending angle, shear displacement, and tibia acceleration. abstract: Rationale. Bioinformatics workflows increasingly need to integrate heterogeneous biomedical data, including experimental assay outputs, patient-derived model metadata, mechanistic models and molecular-pathology information. In glioblastoma (GBM), such integration can help connect treatment responses measured in patient-derived 3D cultures with molecular context and mechanistic representations of tumor metabolism, while maintaining a clear distinction between experimental observations and model-derived hypotheses. Results. We describe a standards-based workflow that integrates patient-derived GBM drug-response screens with a machine-readable QSP model, MGMT promoter methylation metadata and an explicit evidence-tier framework. MGMT-promoter methylation was confirmed in all patient-derived 3D cultures (Ge258, Ge518 and Ge904). Phenformin (PTF) showed the most pronounced single-agent activity, with a concentration-dependent reduction in viability, while 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG) produced a more moderate effect. title: EC-YOLO: a real-time object detection framework for minute bone tumors in X-ray imaging
abstract: Accurate early diagnosis of bone tumors is crucial for optimizing clinical treatment protocols and improving patient prognosis. However, traditional manual evaluation of X-ray images is constrained by blurred lesion boundaries, high missed-detection rates for minute lesions, and insufficient adaptability to multi-scale tumor presentations. Furthermore, manual diagnostic processes lack the real-time efficiency required for clinical workflows. Consequently, these limitations elevate the risks of misdiagnosis and missed detections, rendering traditional methods inadequate for rapid clinical triage and large-scale screening demands. To address these clinical challenges, this study proposes EC-YOLO, an advanced object detection framework built upon the YOLOv11n architecture. The model integrates an Efficient Vision State Space (EVSS) module and a Context-Guided Spatial Reconstruction Feature Pyramid Network (CGRFPN) to facilitate global information capture, spatial feature calibration, and multi-scale fusion. title: Botanical Context Biasing for Experience-Dependent Neuroplasticity: A Two-Timescale Hypothesis of Directional Reinforcement During Psilocybin-Induced Plasticity
abstract: Psilocybin and related psychedelics can induce transient states of increased neural variability, context sensitivity, and plasticity-associated signaling. We hypothesize that selected companion botanicals can be composed with psilocybin to create a reproducible physiological and experiential lens, a botanical context, that biases the qualitative trajectory of the psychedelic state without increasing its pharmacological intensity. In this formulation-level model, psilocybin is the primary compound of experience and changeability, while companion botanicals shape variables such as arousal, autonomic tone, attentional salience, motivational state, interoception, and affect. The prediction is not that botanicals force an outcome, but that they alter the probability distribution of experience in consistent, formulation-specific directions. We further propose that this input operates across two timescales. A tonic layer, established over weeks of continuous administration, sets the stable physiological baseline into which each plasticity window opens and is the principal source of the input’s reproducibility across sessions. title: A K-Means Clustering and Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm-based Routing Framework for Dynamic Communication Networks
abstract: To guarantee dependable and timely data transfer, dynamic communication networks including Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs), Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), Internet of Things (IoT) system, and Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) need effective routing techniques. Because of node mobility, network congestion, energy limitations, and frequent topology changes, conventional routing protocols frequently suffer from performance degradation. This study suggests and optimized routing architecture for dynamic communication networks that combines the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) optimization method with K-Means clustering in order to overcome these difficulties. Network nodes are arranged into effective clusters using the K-Means clustering technique. Which lowers routing overhead and increases network scalability. The Artificial Bee Colony method takes into account factors including residual energy, communication distance, link quality, and network congestion to determine the best cluster heads and find effective routing patterns. Similarly, Shen and Shen (2025) found that employee voice behaviour is encouraged in the organisations that promote an inclusive climate. Their results confirms that organisations with inclusive climates enhance employees' confidence in communicating ideas by enhanced voice efficacy. title: Conservation or Conspiracy? An Operational Criterion for Fine-Tuning in Time-Symmetric Models, with a Symmetry Theorem and a Coincidence-Rate Protocol
abstract: Causal-model arguments establish that a classical causal model reproducing Bell correlations while exhibiting no-signalling must be unfaithful: its no-signalling independences are not entailed by d-separation in the causal graph. Applied to time-symmetric, retrocausal, and all-at-once models, this is the fine-tuning objection. No monotonicity, continuity, differentiability, or power-law assumption is required. Within two-qubit quantum kinematics with ideal analyzer projectors, joint rotational invariance and perfect same-axis anticorrelation force the singlet state and hence this pairing symmetry. title: Perspectives on a pay-for-performance model and its implications for motivation and job performance: insights from primary health care staff in Iran
abstract: Community health workers (CHWs) play a well-documented role in advancing health indicators across Iran. Evidence indicates that financial incentives significantly influence their performance and motivation. Pay-for-performance (P4P) has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance staff motivation and performance. However, little is known about how CHWs themselves perceive this model. This study therefore explored frontline health workers’ perspectives on the P4P system. This qualitative study employed thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s framework. Twenty-five participants, including managers, rural insurance physicians, midwifery experts, and community health workers (CHWs) from the Pakdasht healthcare network, were selected through purposive sampling and recruitment continued until data saturation. Data were collected via semi-structured interviews lasting approximately one hour, guided by an interview protocol. All interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed iteratively to identify codes, subthemes, and themes. Relationships between themes and codes were managed using ATLAS.ti version 7. The analysis identified three overarching dimensions of perfor

title: Economic Sustainability Models of Open Educational Resources (OER) in Developing Regions: A Literature Review
abstract: In resource-constrained higher education institutions (HEIs) and Open and Distance Learning (ODL) systems across developing regions and emerging economies, escalating commercial textbook prices and recurring digital software licensing fees impose severe structural barriers on student access, persistence, and institutional fiscal stability. Open Educational Resources (OER) have emerged as a transformative operational and economic intervention, enabling institutions to replace costly commercial acquisitions with collaborative, openly licensed learning assets. Grounded in the CIMO (Context, Intervention, Mechanism, Outcome) framework, this systematic literature review synthesizes empirical evidence on the economic sustainability models, cost structures, and operational outcomes of OER adoption published between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2025. Comprehensive searches were conducted across five electronic databases—Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, EBSCOhost, ProQuest, and JSTOR. Following a rigorous two-stage screening protocol and critical quality appraisal using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) 2018, 36 empirical studies meeting all eligibility criteria were inclu

title: Protocol: Systematic Literature Review on Multiproduct Lotsizing and Scheduling in Single-Machine Environments: A Theoretical-Empirical Analysis
abstract: Multiproduct lot-sizing and scheduling in single-machine or single-resource environments constitutes a classical and still relevant problem in the field of operations management. It requires coordinating lot-size decisions, production scheduling or sequencing, and the use of a constrained production resource, under setup-related conditions such as setup times, setup costs, and sequence-dependent changeovers. This problem is commonly addressed through the Economic Lot Scheduling Problem (ELSP). Although various models have been developed in the literature, their application in real industrial contexts has been less explored. In this context, the present protocol proposes the design of a systematic literature review aimed at analyzing multiproduct lot-sizing and scheduling in single-machine environments from a theoretical-empirical perspective. In particular, the review will examine the modelling assumptions and methodological approaches used in these studies, the level of empirical or industrial evidence supporting them, the factors influencing their adoption in industrial contexts, and the incorporation of sustainability and resilience criteria. The protocol also defines a structur

title: Quipu: an AI-native knowledge graph with strict ontology enforcement
abstract: An embeddable, governed, bitemporal knowledge-graph store built for agent-written knowledge. No fact enters except through a gate whose predicates evaluate the pending post-state. Data, trust labels, verdicts and the validation rules themselves are bitemporal. Named graphs are the unit of authority and trust, composed under a lattice whose single invariant is that composition never widens. The governance specification, the trace and signed verdicts are facts in the store they govern, which makes the audit a query rather than an external process. Written in Rust. Exposes 28 Model Context Protocol tools. Evaluation harness and census data under benchmark/census/.

title: Execution Governance for AI Orchestration and Agentic Systems
abstract: Execution Governance for AI Orchestration and Agentic Systems v1.1.4 presents a cumulative execution-governance architecture for consequential actions produced by AI orchestration, autonomous agents, sub-agents, tools, protocols, memories, workflows, and effect-producing systems. The central proposition is simple: ability is not authority. Model capability, identity, authentication, credentials, tool access, protocol validity, model confidence, or successful execution do not, by themselves, establish that a particular consequential effect is authorized now. This edition extends the original pre-effect authorization foundation into a cumulative EG3–EG6 architecture specialized for agentic systems. The Six Conditions remain the normative authorization core, while later layers address distinct execution-integrity problems: EG3 — Agentic Commitment Integrity, preserving current authority through the exact action, tool, target, parameters, and release path; EG4 — Agentic Effect Fabric Integrity, preserving rooted, non-expanding, revocable authority across agents, protocols, tools, workloads, services, and effect surfaces; EG5 — Agentic Regime Integrity, governing material changes to pol

title: Editorial: Breaking the cycle: exploring the interplay of conflict, hunger, poverty, and food insecurity in Africa and other regions, and implications for policy
abstract: Attaining the United Nations targets for Sustainable Development Goal 1 (No Poverty) and 2 (Zero Hunger) in less than five years from now (2030), have remained a challenging task for low-and middle-income countries, especially Africa, which hosts the largest number of people (309 million) facing hunger globally in 2025. It was reported that one out of every five people (20%) in Africa face hunger in 2025, compared to 6% of the population in Asia, 4.8% in Latin America and the Caribbean, 8% in Oceania and below 2.5% in Northern America and Europe (1).To understand the structural unity of the 19 papers in this volume, we must establish a clear Systems-Level Conceptual Framework. The interactions among conflict, hunger, poverty, and food insecurity are nonlinear, functioning as a self-reinforcing feedback system of interconnected feedback loops. The systemic complexity of these interactions is illustrated in the conceptual framework presented in Figure 1, which maps the reinforcing feedback loops that either trap households in a self-perpetuating "cycle of vulnerability" or through targeted policy interventions, shift them onto a "virtuous cycle of resilience". title: Quantifying the Environmental Impact of Artisanal and Small‐Scale Mining: An Integrated Approach for Sustainable Development Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Artisanal and small‐scale mining (ASM) provides livelihoods for over 44.5 million people globally, yet its largely unregulated nature causes severe environmental degradation in host communities. In Nigeria, where ASM accounts for over 90% of solid mineral production, the sector increasingly encroaches on agricultural land. Despite growing recognition of ASM's environmental impacts across West Africa, no study has yet applied the novel SDGSAT‐1 satellite purpose‐built for SDG monitoring at 10 m resolution to quantify ASM land degradation in Nigeria, and few studies simultaneously integrate multi‐sensor remote sensing, in‐situ soil contamination assessment, and hydrological transport modelling within a single integrated framework. This study addresses that gap. This study integrates SDGSAT‐1 Multispectral Imager and Landsat 9 imagery (both acquired 12 January 2024) with field‐based soil sampling (November 2023, dry season) and GIS hydrological modelling for Igbojaiye community, Oyo State, Nigeria. Eight vegetation, water and soil indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, TSAVI, TVI, NDWI, BSI) and Land Surface Temperature were derived from satellite imagery. Soil samples from eight mining‐a

title: Constraint-stage diagnosis of transcript-derived reaction scoring in constraint-based metabolic prediction
abstract: Code, protocol records and result tables for a controlled study of the interface between transcript-derived reaction scores and constraint-based metabolic prediction. Measures how often rank-preserving changes to score spacing alter predicted extracellular exchange, locates the modeling stage at which the between-context variation is removed, and tests the resulting reporting rule on an independent condition-response dataset.

title: When Tool Calls Succeed but Workflows Fail: Anomalies at the Agent-Tool Boundary
abstract: AI agents increasingly execute long-running workflows that externalize effects through independently supplied tools. Under retries, speculative execution, concurrency, and partial failures, the resulting external state may be inconsistent with the workflow's intended resolution: required effects may be missing or duplicated, aborted effects may survive, and committed effects may depend on provisional state that is later withdrawn. Advanced transaction models address related failures, but assume that lower-level operations expose the semantics they depend on: whether an effect occurred, whether it can be compensated, staged, or safely reordered. Shared agent-tool interfaces usually do not. We contribute an effect-history model that separates events in the external world from the runtime's observations of them, and a catalog of eight recurring external-effect anomalies. From the catalog we derive the boundary capabilities required to exclude each anomaly in general, and four points where black-box tool invocation alone cannot provide a general guarantee. We then ask how much of this is expressible in a widely used shared tool interface, measuring the use of the standard annotation vo

title: Authorization Architectures for Tool-Using AI Agents
abstract: Tool-using artificial intelligence (AI) agents, systems that autonomously invoke application programming interfaces (APIs), databases, browsers, and inter-agent protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), are becoming production infrastructure. Yet the security model governing when an agent is authorized to act on a human's behalf remains underdeveloped. Trustworthy human-AI systems require that every consequential agent action be traceable to a human principal, bounded by what that human actually delegated, and contestable after the fact; few documented deployments satisfy all three properties reliably and end to end. Existing literature addresses fragments of this problem in isolation, credential management for non-human identities, classical access control models, prompt injection, and audit trails, while giving little attention to the authorization decision point itself, the moment a tool invocation occurs, and mechanisms that make that decision correct, enforceable, and accountable. This review introduces a principal hierarchy spanning human user, operator/deployer, orchestrator agent, sub-agent, and tool endpoint as an organizing framework, and examines five interdepe

title: Beyond Glycemic Control: Periodontal, Salivary, and Oral Mi-crobiome Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists—A Scoping Re-view of Clinical and Preclinical Evidence
abstract: This project comprises a scoping review mapping the clinical and preclinical evidence concerning the effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) on periodontal and peri-implant tissues, salivary function, oral microbial communities, and other clinically relevant oral or orofacial outcomes. The review includes original human, animal in vivo, in vitro/ex vivo, and mixed-design studies and follows the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance. The evidence will be characterized according to study design, population or experimental model, metabolic context, investigated GLP-1RA, comparator, administration protocol, oral-health domain, assessed outcomes, statistical methods, and principal findings. Particular attention will be given to periodontal inflammation, oxidative stress, alveolar bone remodeling, osteogenic differentiation, peri-implant osseointegration, salivary dysfunction, oral microbiome alterations, and orofacial adverse events. Design-specific methodological appraisal will be conducted using the appropriate JBI critical-appraisal checklists for human studies, the SYRCLE risk-of-bias tool for animal investigations, and the QUI

title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
abstract: Reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) provides rich information about evolving surfaces during thin-film growth, but non-automated, operator-dependent alignment and fragmented analysis workflows limit its potential in fully autonomous synthesis. Here, we present an open-source hardware and software toolkit that makes RHEED control and quantitative analysis accessible to operators and artificial intelligence (AI) agents. Demonstrated on a pulsed laser deposition system, the toolkit provides programmable electron-optics control, automated beam alignment and rocking-curve acquisition, and a training-free method for crystallographic azimuthal alignment. The auto RHEED application extracts structural and growth-related observables through shared graphical and programmatic interfaces, including a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. An agent-driven demonstration shows how natural-language requests can guide the selection, configuration, and execution of quantitative analyses. title: Toward Sustainable Technology Transfer in Agriculture: An Intersystemic Model for Emerging Countries
abstract: This study examined how technology transfer has been conceptualized and implemented in agricultural value chains in emerging countries. A systematic literature review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses protocol to analyze 127 peer-reviewed articles retrieved from major scientific databases. The analysis showed a shift from linear diffusion models toward participatory, digital, network-oriented, and systems-innovation approaches, while revealing persistent gaps in feedback mechanisms, cross-system coordination, and the traceability of field evidence within institutional and environmental decision processes. Based on these findings, the study developed the Intersystemic X Model for Sustainable Technology Transfer, a user-centered framework that integrated technical, social, institutional, and environmental subsystems through iterative learning cycles, versioned protocols, and lightweight measurement and verification mechanisms. The model positioned farmers as co-creators and incorporated regulatory and sustainability requirements from the outset. title: Suitability of Delegated and Participatory Leadership Models for Effective Management and Supervision in Public Secondary Schools in Kinondoni Municipality, Tanzania
abstract: Public secondary schools require suitable leadership models, yet authoritarian routines and uneven participation constrain management and supervision. This study examined delegated leadership in Kinondoni Municipality, Tanzania. Its purpose was to generate evidence on leadership arrangements; the main objective was to assess the suitability of leadership models for effective management and supervision. A mixed-methods approach and explanatory sequential design were used. The analysed sample comprised 417 participants: 400 students, eight class teachers, four academic teachers, three head teachers, and two Ward Education Officers from public secondary schools. Questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, observation checklists, and documentary-review guides collected data. Questionnaires were administered first; interviews, observations, and records explained and triangulated patterns. SPSS version 28 produced frequencies, percentages, and means, while qualitative evidence was analysed thematically using Braun and Clarke's six phases. Expert review, construct and face checks, pilot testing, triangulation, and a Cronbach's alpha acceptance criterion of .70 supported validity and relia

title: Incidence of Delayed Discharges in the Maternity Inpatient Unit in a Selected Hospital in Dubai, United Arab Emirates
abstract: This paper examined the incidence and influence of delayed discharges in maternity inpatient units within a private hospital in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, where efficiency and patient satisfaction are critical benchmarks of care. The purpose of the study is to identify the frequency, duration, and underlying causes of discharge delays, and to determine their relationship with contributory factors such as comorbidities and clinical issues. Anchored on Donabedian’s Model of Healthcare Quality and Systems Theory, the research employs a descriptive–correlational design, utilizing a structured questionnaire administered to 40 purposively selected healthcare professionals including nurses, midwives, and physicians. Findings reveal that delayed discharges are a recurring issue, most pronounced among patients requiring extended monitoring and those with maternal or neonatal complications, while administrative bottlenecks such as insurance clearance further exacerbate inefficiencies. Statistical analysis confirmed significant correlations between the incidence of delays and their contributory factors, underscoring the multifactorial nature of the problem. title: Expansion and Growth with the Basic Protocol for Personal and Social Order, an Instrument for Development
abstract: The Pedagogy of Personal and Social Order proposes a framework for examining personal and social order across different community and organizational settings. This methodological and exploratory study aimed to develop a Basic Protocol of Personal and Social Order. The study comprised three main stages: conceptual analysis of basic human needs and social disorder; observational research to examine the principles identified during the conceptual phase; and iterative development and refinement of a pedagogical scale and protocol through successive trial-and-error applications. The resulting protocol addresses three proposed dimensions of personal order: safety and health; appropriate use of truth and avoidance of destructive lies; and responsible management of tangible and intangible resources. The observational and iterative evidence informed the development of the protocol but does not constitute controlled experimental validation. The findings suggest that the proposed protocol may offer a framework for examining and supporting personal and social order in diverse settings. title: Open Forest Observatory Data Catalog
abstract: It is critical that you read this Description document in full prior to any use of the data. The Open Forest Observatory (OFO) Open Data Catalog consists of two components: (1) ground-based manual forest inventory plot data and (2) drone imagery and derived data (e.g. orthomosaics, canopy height models, and maps of automatically detected trees). Many of the ground plots are covered by one or more drone collects, facilitating development and validation of drone-based forest mapping methods. The OFO data catalog is a compilation of contributions from many organizations and individuals. Each data item (e.g. ground-based manual inventory plot; drone collect and derived products) has its own Creative Commons data license, as indicated by the `license` attribute (column) in the associated data/metadata file(s) (see below). The Zenodo data description (the document you are currently reading) describes the data catalog and important usage restrictions and considerations. It is critical that you read this Description document in full prior to any use of the data. title: MCP Data Server
abstract: An open Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects AI agents to cloud-native data. It grounds agents in STAC metadata and confines them to validated cloud-native engines — SQL over Parquet on S3 via DuckDB with H3 spatial indexing — so they can query terabyte-scale data without downloading it, misreading it, or silently failing at scale. Runs locally for sensitive data or on autoscaling Kubernetes for scale.

title: lat — Language as a Tool
abstract: A local, read-only Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that serves a curated catalogue of natural-language and poetic "thinking patterns", classified by a closed set of cognitive axes, for reframing a problem through a contrasting language or form. The selection method is an inverted soft Sapir-Whorf model: the grammatical bias of the input language is treated not as a constraint on the speaker but as a choosable instrument, and a structurally orthogonal pattern is selected because it forces the distinction the input language leaves implicit.

title: Replication data and code for: Modelling hunters' perceptions, cognitive-affective image and loyalty in Sierra Morena driven-hunt tourism
abstract: RESEARCH PROTOCOL for the Cognitive-Affective-Conative (CA) Mediation Model's Hunting Tourism This dataset and analysis code accompany a study examining whether the cognitive-affective(-conative) model of destination image — widely validated in cultural, sun-and-beach, ecotourism, and adventure-tourism contexts — extends to hunting tourism, a specialised and socially controversial activity where image formation has not previously been tested under this framework.Survey data were collected from 288 hunters and participants at eleven driven hunts (monterías) held on hunting estates across Sierra Morena, Córdoba province, Spain, between October 2025 and February 2026. A structural equation model (estimated in JASP/lavaan, MLR estimator, FIML for missing data) specifies hunting-specific motivation (MOT) as a predictor of a second-order cognitive image of the hunting experience (CIH) — itself built from hunting effectiveness, infrastructure and accessibility, and service quality and hospitality — which in turn predicts satisfaction (STS) and, jointly with satisfaction, destination loyalty (LYL).All four hypothesised structural paths were supported: motivation significantly predicted cog

title: From Self-Protection to Experiential Engagement: A State-Dependent Autonomic Model of Psychotherapy Process
abstract: This conceptual and clinical article introduces the State-Dependent Autonomic Response Model (SDARM), a transtheoretical framework for understanding moment-to-moment client responses during psychotherapy. The model addresses a common clinical challenge: as clients approach painful emotions, attachment injuries, traumatic memories, maladaptive schemas, or other forms of core suffering, their responses may shift in ways that make therapeutic work difficult. They may criticize themselves or others, argue, search for someone to blame, overanalyze, intellectualize, change the subject, become preoccupied with abstract psychological, philosophical, spiritual, or social explanations, fall silent, experience mental blankness, withdraw, become numb, or lose access to emotional and bodily experience. Different psychotherapy traditions describe these phenomena using constructs such as dysfunctional thoughts, cognitive distortions, rumination, resistance, defense mechanisms, experiential avoidance, self-criticism, process markers, coping modes, self-interruption, or protective parts. Although each of these concepts can be clinically valuable, the large number of approach-specific classification

title: Chromosomes deconstructed
abstract: As is argued in chapter 1 – to study the organization of mitotic chromosomes it does not suffice to simply observe their formation through a microscope: the relevant processes occur at scales below the diffraction limit. This thesis presents three experimental approaches that circumvent the problem of optical resolution limits in creative ways; all using a combination of fluorescence microscopy and optical tweezers. Chapter 2 presents experiments to study the heterogeneity of mechanical properties throughout the chromosome. In order to study their mechanical heterogeneity, chromosomes are stretched using optical tweezers, while the extensions of fluorescently labeled components or segments of the chromosomes are monitored using STED super-resolution fluorescence microscopy. First, the stiffness of the centromeres is compared to that of the bulk of the chromosome. To this end, centromeres are immunofluorescently labeled, and during longitudinal chromosome stretches, their extension is monitored using STED. Centromeres turn out to be exceptionally soft: an order of magnitude softer than the whole chromosome. This finding is placed in the context of the recent finding that centromeres

title: Rohan: A Stateless Zero-Knowledge Trust Gateway for Privacy-Preserving Agentic Workflows via Streamable HTTP
abstract: The rapid advance of autonomous Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) across enterprise workflows, AI infrastructure increasingly transitions toward cloud-native, scale-to-zero environments and browser-native execution runtimes. However, production deployment remains severely constrained by data leakage risks inherent to the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which frequently exchanges sensitive credentials, system prompts, and negotiation constraints in plaintext. Furthermore, legacy security boundaries enforce persistent network tunnels (e.g., Server-Sent Events, WebSockets) that break serverless scalability. title: A Lightweight Defense Architecture Against Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Calling AI Agents
abstract: The rapid integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into autonomous agent workflows has introduced significant security challenges, most notably Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI). As agents increasingly rely on external tools and protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data from APIs, web searches, and databases, untrusted content can subvert the agent’s core instructions, leading to unauthorized actions. While foundation-model evaluators offer a potential defense, their deployment is often hindered by high inference latency (400–1200 ms) and substantial operational costs. This paper proposes a lightweight multi-stage guardrail architecture, "LightGuard-Agent," designed to secure the tool-calling loop without compromising system performance. Our approach utilizes a tiered defense pipeline, ranging from deterministic syntactic sanitization to high-speed semantic intent classification and an execution policy action firewall. title: MCP Data Server
abstract: An open Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects AI agents to cloud-native data. It grounds agents in STAC metadata and confines them to validated cloud-native engines — SQL over Parquet on S3 via DuckDB with H3 spatial indexing — so they can query terabyte-scale data without downloading it, misreading it, or silently failing at scale. Runs locally for sensitive data or on autoscaling Kubernetes for scale.

title: Measuring Coping Strategies in Daily Life: A Systematic Review of Experience Sampling Methodology and Daily Diary Studies
abstract: Advances in daily diary methods and experience sampling method (ESM) have improved the study of coping strategies in daily life and their role in shaping health and well-being. In this review, we examine study designs, measurement approaches, and analytical practices used to investigate coping in natural contexts. We performed a systematic review of studies published before 5 December 2025 that used daily diary or ESM to measure coping strategies over multiple days or moments. Studies were examined with regard to sampling schemes, assessment frequency and duration, measurement of coping strategies, incorporation of stressor appraisals, and analytic techniques used to model coping processes. Fifty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. Results indicated that 80% employed end-of-day diary designs, generally lasting 1-3 weeks, whereas higher-frequency ESM protocols were less common and ranged 2-14 days. Coping strategies were often assessed using abbreviated or single-item measures, frequently adapted from established questionnaires. title: GLAL v0.9 — Governance Layer for Agentic AI
abstract: GLAL v0.9 — Governance Layer for Agentic AI presents a vendor-neutral reference architecture for governing agentic AI systems across local, private, air-gapped, and controlled hybrid environments. Its central principle is that increasing cognitive capability must not automatically increase operational authority. GLAL therefore separates the Intelligence Plane, where models interpret information, retrieve context, reason, plan, and propose actions, from an independent Authority Plane, responsible for identity, evidence validation, policy enforcement, authorization, execution constraints, post-action verification, and auditability. Version 0.9 extends this architecture with two additional governance boundaries. The first is an Epistemic Gate, based on the principle that greater uncertainty should contract rather than expand permissible authority: insufficient verified evidence should lead to abstention, evidence retrieval, recommendation-only operation, or human escalation rather than execution based on model confidence alone.
