title: From Mathematics Anxiety to Critical Thinking
abstract: Mathematics anxiety can constrain cognitive engagement and critical thinking in calculus, while Artificial Intelligence (AI) creates opportunities for personalised learning, problem solving, and STEM innovation. This chapter synthesises evidence on mathematics anxiety, critical thinking, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), contextual learning, and AI-supported STEM education through a Systematic Literature Review following PRISMA 2020. Searches across Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, Dimensions, and additional sources identified 2,700 records, with 191 studies meeting the inclusion criteria. The synthesis shows that quantitative studies (58.6%), higher education (72.3%), mathematics education (42.9%), and Asian contexts (46.6%) dominate the literature. Mathematics anxiety emerges as a barrier to cognitive engagement, whereas contextual learning, SDG-oriented tasks, and AI-supported learning can strengthen relevance, problem solving, personalisation, and critical thinking. The chapter positions REALMATH-SDGs as a contextual framework linking affective support, and critical thinking.

title: From observation to autonomous discovery: An epistemic-capability framework for artificial intelligence in food science
Ethical AI in Practice
abstract: The swift incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) into science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education has generated revolutionary prospects for customized learning, intelligent tutoring, predictive analytics, and automated evaluation. But with these benefits come important ethical issues that have to do with governance, openness, responsibility, prejudice, privacy, and responsible innovation. This chapter looks at how Ethical AI is changing in STEM education by looking at real-world case studies that show both good and bad uses of AI-powered educational technology. The chapter starts by putting AI in the context of modern STEM education systems. It talks about how data-driven decision-making, adaptive learning platforms, and AI-powered analytics are changing the way teachers and students learn. These technologies may lead to better learning and more efficient use of resources, but they also make people worry about things like algorithmic bias, unclear decision-making processes, monitoring of student data, and unfair access to AI tools. The chapter examines how educational institutions, technology creators, and legislators are dealing with the ethical issue

title: Artificial Intelligence Derived from Ancient Indian Practices in Chemistry
abstract: This chapter explores the intersection between the Ancient Indian Practices (AIP) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), highlighting the relevance of the traditional Indian Knowledge System (IKS) to the advancement of chemical sciences. The vast data of the Indian Knowledge System are available in the form of textual materials (i.e., manuscripts, stone inscriptions, palm leaves, copper plates), oral traditions and rituals, religious practices, archaeological sources, inscriptions, and more. This plethora of data can be effectively utilized to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI) model to understand and give a new perspective into these old practices. The chapter begins with a brief overview of the ancient Indian Knowledge System related to the chemical sciences. It further explains the basics of AI including machine learning, data modeling, pattern detection, predictive analytics, and algorithmic decision-making. It explores how AI tools can help to standardize traditional chemical formulations, search 207 through ancient knowledge to discover new drugs, or make personalized treatments more effective and accurate. It also emphasizes the potential benefits and challenges along with t

title: Marketing Analytics for Gastrointestinal Cancer Prevention and Early Detection: Emerging Trends, Analytical Frameworks and Research Directions
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, such as colorectal, gastric, liver, pancreatic, and oesophageal cancers, continue to represent a serious public health concern because of their high prevalence and mortality and frequent delayed diagnosis. The evolution of marketing analytics offers new opportunities to address existing barriers to prevention and early diagnosis through evidence-based decision-making, tailored communication, and screening interventions. This narrative review analyses the current state of marketing analytics applications in GI cancer prevention and early detection, with a focus on social marketing, behavioural models, artificial intelligence (AI), digital health, and emerging marketing analytics approaches. The epidemiological landscape of GI cancers, prevention and screening methods, marketing analytics tools and analytical frameworks supporting patient engagement and screening uptake, and recent developments, including AI, big data, precision marketing, explainable AI, social media analytics, and real-time analytics, are reviewed in the context of current research challenges and gaps. The review indicates that integrating marketing analytics with behavioural science

title: Integrating Generative AI in STEM Projects
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools—most notably large language models such as ChatGPT—are rapidly reshaping the landscape of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. This chapter examines the dual role of GenAI in STEM project-based learning: as a pedagogical enabler and a source of risk. Drawing on a synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2021 and 2025, the chapter identifies key opportunities including personalized learning, adaptive feedback, scaffolded inquiry, and increased instructional efficiency. It also examines risks such as academic dishonesty, algorithmic bias, data privacy violations, and equity gaps. Ethical frameworks for responsible GenAI integration are proposed, emphasizing AI literacy, transparent policy design, and teacher development. The chapter concludes that sustainable GenAI adoption in STEM requires not just technological fluency, but a principled, equity-centered pedagogical commitment from stakeholders.

title: The Italian Nanomedicine Platform (INP): national integration within the European nanomedicine ecosystem
abstract: Italy's nanomedicine expertise has long developed in fragmented manner, with limited coordination across academia, clinical institutions, industry and regulatory bodies. The Italian Nanomedicine Platform (INP) was established to integrate discovery, preclinical validation, regulatory science and industrial translation within a single ecosystem aligned with Horizon Europe Cluster 1. We report the proceedings of the First INP Meeting (Rome, 16-18 Feb 2026), encompassing keynote contributions from European and international leaders, a national pitch session mapping institutional capabilities, and results from a structured inaugural survey. The meeting gathered ~140 principal investigators from nearly 100 institutions and formalized eight thematic Working Groups. A subsequent registration round reached 170 participants from 109 institutions. Over 60% of declared activity concerns nanomedicine products, physicochemical characterization, cell-based models and imaging, whereas regulatory science, AI and Health Technology Assessment remain under-represented (10-25%). The Technology Readiness Level distribution is markedly skewed toward early stages (~80% at TRL 1-4). Keynote speakers ident

title: Self-generated goals in the age of foundation models: artificial autotelic agents and their implications for cognitive science
abstract: Goals have traditionally been treated as inputs to intelligent systems, biological and artificial, rather than as products of intelligence itself. A growing body of work in cognitive science and artificial intelligence (AI) challenges this framing through autotelic agents — self-improving systems motivated to represent, generate, select, and pursue their own goals. Recent advances in foundation models (large-scale generative AI models trained on broad datasets) expand this research program by extending the languages and tools through which artificial agents can express, evaluate, and pursue goals. By operating over formats such as natural language and code, foundation models allow agents to generate more abstract and compositional goals, approximate human judgments of interestingness and learnability, and support richer loops of problem generation and problem solving. These advances create new opportunities for cognitive science to model human goal dynamics, for AI to build more adaptive autotelic systems, and for human–AI systems to support shared goal exploration without narrowing human agency.

title: Retina as a window to systemic hypertension: From hypertensive retinopathy to artificial intelligence-driven microvascular biomarkers
abstract: The retinal microvasculature is the only vascular bed in the human body that can be visualised directly, non-invasively and repeatedly in vivo . Because retinal arterioles share embryological origin, calibre and autoregulatory physiology with the cerebral and coronary microcirculation, hypertension-induced retinal changes offer a unique window onto systemic small-vessel disease. For this narrative minireview, PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore were searched from database inception to April 30, 2026 for peer-reviewed English-language human studies of hypertensive retinopathy, quantitative retinal vascular biomarkers, multimodal retinal imaging and artificial intelligence (AI) applied to fundus images; population-based cohorts, individual-participant meta-analyses and AI studies reporting external validation were prioritised, and evidence was synthesised thematically and tabulated for cross-study comparison. Classical hypertensive retinopathy, graded for over eight decades by the Keith-Wagener-Barker and Scheie systems, has been supplemented by quantitative measurement of retinal vessel calibre and by geometric parameters such as fractal dimension and tort

title: Data science skills as integrators: diffusion of the algorithmic power in contemporary Chinese labor market
abstract: Data science-related skills are transforming Chinese labor market in the AI era. By conceptualizing the labor market as a dynamic skill network, we argue that data science skills act as integrators, connecting previously disconnected domain-specific skill clusters across different occupations and consolidating algorithmic control. Using a large-scale dataset of high-skill job postings from liepin.com, we leverage LLM-based data extraction, classification, and network analysis to trace the diffusion of data science skills and their integration with two occupations leading this diffusion in the labor market: biomedicine and finance. Results demonstrate a marked increase in network density and the inter-occupational ties between data science and the other two occupations from 2015 to 2023, integrated by a few key skills in data science. The effect of data science skills on inter-occupational integration exceeds that of the overall network density growth. Making progress in using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to solve the extreme multilabel text classification (XMTC) problem in large-scale, unstructured Chinese textual data at the job level, our analyses illustrate how data scie

title: The Ethical AI in AI Sociology
abstract: This chapter underscores the need for an ethical AI, grounded not solely in computer science, but in a perceptive and philosophical understanding of how social forces influence technology. Employing a Bourdieusian lens, among others, to the codes linking our digital society may demonstrate how redesigning ethical standards can challenge structural racism and systemic inequities, which existing AI models repeatedly typify. This chapter includes several theoretical frameworks (ethical AI as a sociopolitical phenomenon, inclusive of Social Construction of Technology, Actor-Network Theory, and technological determinism; Critical Theory, inclusive of power relations, reproduction of inequality, and ethics washing; and a shift from prescriptive to critical/reflexive task), intending to present an understanding of the multi-layered relationship between AI and society. These sociological tools are essential for any inquiry into when and how inequalities are made stronger by AI systems because AI sociology has shifted the center from targeting technical errors to targeting the unequal distribution of power and resources grounded within society&s;s institutions and systems.

title: Large language models in healthcare: applications, evaluation frameworks, and governance pathways — a scoping review and multidimensional framework
abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated for healthcare applications spanning clinical documentation, decision support, patient communication, research assistance, and operational workflows. Despite rapid adoption interest, evidence remains heterogeneous and standardised approaches for evaluation and governance are not yet consistently applied. Objective To map healthcare applications of LLMs, synthesise reported outcomes and risks, and propose a multidimensional evaluation and governance framework oriented toward digital-health implementation. Methods A scoping review was conducted following the methodological guidance of Arksey and O'Malley, Levac et al., and the Joanna Briggs Institute, with reporting aligned to the PRISMA-ScR checklist. The protocol was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/SWP78 ). Searches were performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and the ACL Anthology, supplemented by medRxiv/bioRxiv preprint searches and grey-literature scanning of WHO, FDA, and EU AI-Office guidance, covering 1 January 2019–30 April 2026. Title/abstract and f

title: AI-Enabled Learning Analytics and Digital Pedagogy for Sustainable Higher Education Decision-Making
abstract: This chapter develops an AI-enabled learning analytics framework for sustainable higher education decision-making. Responding to fragmented institutional data environments, it integrates learning management, student information, feedback, advising, intervention, progression, and quality assurance data through enterprise architecture logic. Using a design-science orientation, the framework is presented as a conceptual artefact and illustrated through a synthetic dataset of 500 student-course records. The demonstration shows how descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, intervention, feedback, and pathway analytics can function as human-reviewed decision-support signals rather than automated judgements. The chapter emphasizes privacy, transparency, fairness, explainability, governance, and stakeholder oversight, while distinguishing synthetic proof-of-concept outputs from empirical validation. It contributes a responsible model linking analytics, digital pedagogy, student support, and institutional strategy, and identifies future requirements for real-data validation.

title: Toward child-centred ai urbanism: a bibliometric and systematic review of public space and human-centred architecture
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly transformed architectural and urban research through data-driven modelling, spatial analytics, and decision-support systems. Despite this growth, limited attention has been given to human-centred perspectives, particularly children’s spatial experiences, well-being, and ergonomic needs in public environments. This imbalance raises questions about whose needs are represented within AI-supported urban research. This study examines the intersection of AI, architecture, urban design, and public space through bibliometric analysis and a PRISMA-guided systematic review. An initial dataset of 871 publications from Web of Science and Scopus was screened, resulting in 39 studies. A supplementary child-oriented search identified 11 studies, of which four addressed child-related spatial considerations. Findings reveal that existing research is dominated by urban analytics, machine learning, and performance-oriented approaches, while child-centred perspectives remain underrepresented. Comparison between AI-assisted clustering and manual thematic classification shows that automated approaches capture dominant trends but often overlook socially relev

title: GenVR-DSA
abstract: An Interactive VR Platform with GenAI Support for Learning Data Structures is a new educational tool that uses virtual reality to improve the understanding of abstract computer science concepts. The need for such a tool arises from the challenge of understanding abstract concepts of Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) faced by students. This new educational tool combines virtual reality with AI and aims to make the process of understanding data structures more intuitive and interactive. The AI technology will enable the creation of educational content on the fly as students engage with the educational tool. This educational tool will also enable a 3D experience that will allow students to perform various actions on different data structures. The system will provide a multi-sensory experience to the students where they can view as well as perform various actions on the data structures in a 3D reality. The aim of the new educational tool will be to increase the students' understanding of data structures and enable them to implement data structure concepts on a real-world scenario.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Regulatory Science: Opportunities, Challenges, and Emerging Frameworks
Surgical site infections in canine tibial plateau leveling osteotomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background: Surgical site infections (SSIs) following canine tibial plateau leveling osteotomy (TPLO) represent a significant clinical concern. A universal estimate of SSI incidence and identification of predisposing factors can guide preventive strategies. Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (ie, PRISMA) guidelines. Studies reporting outcomes of TPLO procedures published between January 2000 and August 2024 were included. AGRICOLA, BIOSIS Previews, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, PubMed, Scopus, VetMed Resource, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched on August 23, 2024. The AVMA Clinical Trials Registry, International Veterinary Information Service, and World Organisation for Animal Health were searched on September 21, 2024. Two gray literature sources, American College of Veterinary Surgeons Surgery Summit Abstracts and Veterinary Orthopedic Society Conference Abstract Archive, were hand-searched by subject experts on the same date. Studies were excluded if they did not examine dogs that had undergone TPLO surgery, were written in a language other tha

title: Artificial intelligence in science education for SDG 4: A systematic review of AI interventions for ESD and 21st-century competencies
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming science education and creating new opportunities to advance education for sustainable development. This systematic literature review followed the preferred reporting items for systematic review 2020 guidelines to examine 43 empirical studies published in prominent journals between January 2020 and July 2026. Studies were synthesized using descriptive and thematic analyses. Publications increased markedly, with 76.7% appearing during 2024-2025. Quantitative approaches predominated (51.2%), followed by mixed methods (23.3%), qualitative (18.6%), and research and development (7.0%). AI interventions included generative AI, AI-augmented instructional design, AI-supported assessment, immersive environments, adaptive learning systems, and AIoT, supporting critical thinking, scientific reasoning, systems thinking, collaboration, AI literacy, and sustainability awareness. Despite challenges related to equitable access, teacher readiness, and ethical implementation, AI demonstrates strong potential to enhance sustainability-oriented science education. These findings highlight current research trends, methodological gaps, and future directions for

title: A Hybrid COBIT 2019–RAG Framework to Enhance Consumer Protection Compliance in Digital Finance
abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial services has increased the need for effective regulatory compliance mechanisms, particularly for consumer protection. This study develops and evaluates a hybrid COBIT 2019–Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for compliance with Indonesia’s OJK Regulation No. 22/2023 in a digital multifinance context. Using a design science research methodology, COBIT 2019 design factors were applied to tailor governance objectives, while a RAG pipeline was evaluated on 100 synthetic compliance queries using RAGAS metrics and expert-validated reference answers. The governance assessment prioritized EDM03, APO12, and MEA03, each assessed at capability Level 2 against a target of Level 4, indicating gaps in risk optimization, risk management, and external compliance. The optimal RAG configuration achieved an overall score of 0.8257, with context recall of 0.9217, faithfulness of 0.8502, and semantic similarity of 0.8629. It also outperformed baseline keyword search in retrieving semantically relevant regulatory passages, although broader benchmarking remains limited. The findings show that integrating structured IT governance with AI-assisted regulatory

title: Peer Review Report For: Combining Implementation and Data Sciences to Accelerate Evidence Integration into Healthcare – ImpleMATE [version 3; peer review: 1 approved, 2 approved with reservations]
abstract: Background The translation of research evidence into routine healthcare practice is often slow and inconsistent, even timely implementation can significantly improve patient outcomes. While implementation science offers strategies to close this gap, current approaches are frequently manual, fragmented, and poorly integrated within healthcare systems. To address these challenges, we propose ImpleMATE – an AI-assisted implementation science platform designed to streamline implementation efforts. Grounded in the Learning Health System (LHS) model, ImpleMATE aims to establish a continuous, data-driven cycle of learning and improvement in implementation practice. Methods ImpleMATE will be developed through a co-design and co-production approach rooted in human-centred design principles. Development will proceed through four key activities: (1) establishing a data processing pipeline and building an implementation-focused ontology; (2) creating and validating an AI system to extract implementation knowledge, structure the ontology, and support implementation solution delivery; (3) designing an interactive web application to deliver AI-assisted decision support and streamline implementati

title: Development of an automated evaluation system for the process-structure-property relationship of structural metallic materials towards autonomous exploration
abstract: Automated autonomous experiment systems in material science are desired for exploring numerous conditions but barely any examples for solid bulk metals are reported. In this study, an automated experimental system for structural metallic materials is designed to evaluate the process-structure-property relationship of structural metallic materials. Fully automated heat treatments, X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements and impact testing on bulk metallic samples with a size of 40 × 4 × 1.5 mm3 are realized by integrating a robot arm. The experimental process, excluding heat treatment, can be finished within 800 s for 1 sample. Automated high-throughput experiments on the one- and two-step tempering of a JIS SCM435H alloy are performed to demonstrate the capability and efficiency of the system, and the accuracy of the resulting property data is validated by manually measured hardness. It is also found that the diffraction peak width is positively correlated with strength, indicating the capability of the system to achieve structure–property relationships. An AI optimization tool built in the NIMS Orchestration System (NIMO) is implemented, thereby providing a basis for future closed-lo

title: A data-driven comparative analysis on citation intents across scientific disciplines
abstract: The goal of this paper is to conduct a first comparative analysis on citation intents across multiple scientific disciplines. To this end, we conducted a data-driven investigation into the characteristics of citation intents utilizing a large-scale dataset of 17,717 academic papers and 2,345,674 citation contexts from 21 Web of Science subject categories. We analyzed five key characteristics: i) inter-category distribution of citation intents, ii) average number of citation intents per article, iii) age distribution of citation intents, iv) similarity of the age distributions of citation intent, and v) predictability of the number of citation intents. We found out that there are significant differences in all five characteristics across different research disciplines. Specifically, Philosophy, Sociology, Area, and History prioritize Background and Motivation intents while exhibiting minimal engagement with Uses and Extends. Conversely, Computer Science AI represents a unique case, characterized by a dominant prevalence of Uses and Extends intents alongside the least frequent use of background-oriented citations. title: From access to engagement: AI literacy, technological play and academic libraries as sociotechnical learning environments
abstract: Purpose This study examines how academic libraries can support AI literacy through technological play, informal learning, librarian mediation and technology-rich spaces. It argues that AI literacy is sociotechnical: access to tools is necessary but does not by itself produce meaningful participation. The study also considers how institutional resources, governance and professional authority shape who can develop, support and benefit from AI-related learning. Design/methodology/approach Using a qualitative critical interpretive design, the study analyzes library and information science scholarship, professional frameworks, and selected institutional and higher education documents published between 2010 and 2026. Critical discourse analysis identifies recurring narratives of innovation, access, experimentation and professional responsibility. A political-economy lens examines the material and organizational conditions including funding, staffing, infrastructure, professional development, workload and governance that enable or constrain participation. Findings Four interrelated patterns emerge. Academic libraries are framed as sites of technological promise and innovation; librarians

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Development of Critical Thinking in Science Education: A Systematic Review
abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has positioned it as a key driver of digital transformation and changes in learning paradigms. This study systematically examines how AI influences the development of critical thinking in science education, focusing on both underlying mechanisms and instructional practices. Guided by the PRISMA framework, a comprehensive search, screening, and synthesis of literature published between 2021 and 2025 in the Web of Science and Scopus databases were conducted, resulting in a final sample of 21 studies. The findings indicate a sustained growth in research within this field, with mixed-methods approaches predominating. At the technological level, generative AI and adaptive learning systems are the most widely applied, while learning analytics systems, predictive AI, explainable AI, and virtual simulation environments are also gaining increasing attention, forming a complementary and evolving technological ecosystem. At the pedagogical level, AI has become increasingly embedded in instructional design, encompassing teaching models, methods, frameworks, and instructional modules, reflecting a trend toward deeper integration.

title: Foreword
Artificial Intelligence–Driven Discovery of Plant-Derived Bioactive Compounds in Cancer Therapeutics: Computational Approaches and Molecular Target Identification
abstract: Objective: Artificial intelligence (AI) use and computational approaches have transformed the discovery of plant-derived bioactive chemicals for cancer treatment. This review synthesized evidence on AI-based approaches, including network pharmacology, molecular docking, and machine learning, for identifying and validating anticancer plant-derived phytochemicals, focusing on their molecular targets and signaling pathways. Data Sources: PRISMA 2020 guidelines were followed. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched between October 2020 and July 2025. Study Selection: Studies with at least one AI or computational method, investigating plant-derived phytochemicals for anticancer effects, reporting quantitative computational outcomes, and offering free full-text access in English were included. Review articles, conference abstracts, non-plant studies, and non-English publications were excluded. Data Extraction: Two reviewers extracted data on predefined variables. An adapted PROBAST tool was used to assess risk of bias for in silico studies and modified SYRCLE tools for in vitro and in vivo studies, with certainty of evidence evaluated using the GRADE method. title: Use of artificial intelligence for computer aided drug designing
Problem-solving ontologies on steroids? The space for critique in policy research on artificial intelligence
abstract: This article critically examines social sciences research on AI and policy as a politics of knowledge production, offering three key contributions. First, it debates the merit of systematic reviews in critical policy research in revealing epistemic hierarchies and biases. Second, it introduces a heuristic to map the disjointed methodologies of AI-policy scholarship across two ontological dimensions: whether AI features as a neutral problem-solving tool or a socio-technical system shaping power relations; and whether technology serves as a governance instrument or a regulatory target. This framework provides a reflexive, yet systematic, tool to expose epistemic hierarchies and the relative space for critical social scientific engagement. Third, I present findings from a systematic review of 229 English-language articles published in social sciences journals through 2025. Results show a pronounced imbalance: three-quarters of studies focus on AI regulation, while empirical research on technology uses in governance remains marginal. Unified Theistic Naturalism™
abstract: Opening The Checkpoint There are moments in the development of an idea when the individual writings cease to appear as separate works. A paper becomes a doorway into another paper. A book gathers several discoveries that were first encountered independently. A podcast gives voice to a structure that had already been written, tested, observed, and carried through life. Concepts that once appeared local begin connecting across relationships, theology, philosophy, memory, suffering, biology, justice, artificial intelligence, and the ordinary decisions of a human day. Eventually, the shelf changes. What first looked like a collection begins to reveal an architecture. Unified Theistic Naturalism™ has reached such a moment. By this checkpoint, the work has expanded into approximately fifteen books, more than sixty white papers, and more than twenty podcast works. Yet those numbers alone say almost nothing about what has occurred. The significance is not volume. It is convergence. The white papers have served as the primary ground of discovery. title: Ground-State Motion with Complex Interactions: A quadratic propagation limit without a spectral gap
abstract: This technical note derives long-wavelength quantum evolution on the entire ground subspace of a lattice Hamiltonian with bounded hopping. A normal ground state at a global momentum minimum is sufficient: a spectral gap, a real basis, a positive ground function and nearby moving ground eigenvectors are not required. The effective quadratic operator is the direct momentum response minus the relaxation into internal and field excitations. The proof uses the one-variable operator Fejer-Riesz theorem of Dritschel and Rovnyak, together with closed-form convergence. Significance within Recognition Science. The result turns the exact current-response expression into a derived law of motion for the complex native source coupled to the complete reciprocal photon field, with all modes and occupations retained. This connects the existing ground-state result to the calculation of inertial response using the same operator and common units. Strict positivity and numerical evaluation of that response, physical source selection, and particle species and mass assignments remain open. Significance for broader science. title: Finite Ground Spaces in a Complete Photon Field: Existence at every minimizing momentum with complex native interactions
abstract: For the reciprocal lattice field with a finite complex internal interaction, this technical note derives a normal ground state at every global momentum minimum and compactness of the union of all normalized exact ground states across those minima. One finite family of probes detects every ground state with a uniform positive bound on retained norm. The resulting quadratic kinetic response is a finite Hermitian matrix. The photon field retains all modes and occupations. Significance within Recognition Science. This reduces the ground-state part of the full-field particle-spectrum calculation to finite matrix structure at every minimizing momentum, using the same complex native operator and common energy units. It supplies a structural step toward calculating inertial response. The actual dimension, positive kinetic coefficients, physical source selection, bare-source overlap, and particle identities and masses remain to be derived. Significance for broader science. The result separates a finite exact ground space from a spectral gap: arbitrarily soft photons can remove the gap while the exact ground states remain uniformly finite dimensional. title: Enterprise AI Success Metrics: Why Most Projects Fail
abstract: A 94% accurate model means nothing if nobody defined what business outcome it should drive. David Ohnstad exposes the critical gap between data science validation and executive expectations that derails nine months of enterprise AI development. title: Because Data Happens. FAIR data, infrastructure and AI for data-driven biodiversity research. Presentation by SciLifeLab Data Centre.
abstract: Slides from an invited presentation delivered at the Evolutionary Biology Centre (EBC), Uppsala University, on 15 September 2026. The talk introduces researchers in evolution, biodiversity and related fields to the data management support, infrastructure and services offered by the SciLifeLab Data Centre and the NBIS Data Management team, framed around FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles and Open Science. Structured along the research data life cycle — the presentation covers: why good research data management and metadata matter for biodiversity data; FAIR and metadata standards; Data Management Plans and the Data Stewardship Wizard (DSW); Swedish and international infrastructure for biodiversity data; SciLifeLab services (Data Repository/FigShare instance, Serve, Protocols, FAIR Storage, RDM Guidelines); compute and storage through NAISS; the tension between open sharing and data protection for sensitive species observations; the role of AI in data-driven biodiversity research; and available training and bioinformatics support.

title: The Terrorism Enablement Triangle: A conceptual model of intent, capability and resources in an era of AI-augmented threats
abstract: Terrorism assessments have long paired intent with capability, while threat and opportunity models add situational conditions and structured professional judgement frameworks address engagement, resources and protective factors. This paper proposes the Terrorism Enablement Triangle (TET), a conceptual model that treats intent, capability and resources as three interacting actor-centred dimensions of terrorist-action feasibility, with opportunity as the surrounding operating environment. A structured conceptual review identifies relevant prior art in threat triangles, engagement–intent–capability frameworks, crime-science opportunity models and resource-mobilisation accounts. TET’s contribution is a bounded re-specification: it distinguishes an actor’s competence from the assets available to them and separates beliefs, grievances and engagement from violent intent, mobilisation and action. The paper examines three possible ways AI could affect enablement: influence on intent through personalised interaction, capability uplift through task assistance, and resource compression through automation or reduced time, labour and specialist input. It proposes questions for empirical testing.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Surgical Decision-Making in Stoma Formation, Reversal, and Parastomal Hernia Prevention in Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Systematic Review
abstract: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications across the stoma-related surgical decision pathway in colorectal cancer surgery. Unlike prior and ongoing reviews that address single, isolated outcomes, this review integrates three causally and clinically linked domains: (1) the decision to create or omit a temporary diverting stoma, where AI-guided decision-making has already been validated in a randomized controlled trial (Shao et al., Nature Communications, 2026); (2) prediction of permanent stoma or stoma non-reversal, including successful sphincter-preserving resection as its clinical inverse; and (3) prediction and prevention of parastomal hernia or stoma-site incisional hernia. The rationale for this integrated scope is that the temporary-diversion decision directly determines the population at risk for downstream permanent-stoma and hernia outcomes, making these three domains parts of a single decision continuum rather than independent research questions. title: The Power of Didactic Thinking: Frameworks, Cognitive Architecture, and Computational Paradigms in Modern Pedagogy and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Didactic thinking is the intentional and systematic management of knowledge transformation, which involves addressing structural translation of complex information for optimal cognitive assimilation. This concept goes beyond content delivery. Classical pedagogy has been the foundation of didactic thinking, but contemporary cognitive science and computational paradigms have exposed the more structural aspects of this thinking. The paper provides a thorough examination of didactic thinking, emphasizing its relevance in human cognitive structures and autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) systems. We trace the epistemological roots of didactics, operationalize its cognitive underpinnings (working memory constraints, cognitive load theory, and schema construction) and analyze its structural instantiation in machine learning through curriculum learning, prompt engineering, or chain-of-thought prompting. title: Temporal Information, Postmortem Accountability, and the Search for an Empirical Afterlife: A Literature Review
abstract: This paper proposes a technology-oriented research roadmap for investigating whether advanced physics, quantum information science, artificial intelligence, and consciousness research could eventually enable new forms of temporal information retrieval and postmortem accountability. It reviews quantum state reconstruction, reversible quantum dynamics, indefinite causal order, Many-Worlds interpretations, computational historical reconstruction, near-death experiences, terminal lucidity, and anomalous information-reception research. The proposed research architecture progresses from experimentally tractable technologies—AI-assisted historical reconstruction, quantum information recovery, reversible computation, and controlled consciousness-at-death experiments—to more speculative objectives, including information retrieval from the past, cross-timeline information exchange, investigation of postmortem consciousness, and empirical testing of whether moral accountability or reparative processes could exist beyond biological death. title: Claim–Evidence Audit Protocol (CEAP) A Contrastive Reporting Layer for Black-Box AI Evaluation
abstract: The Claim–Evidence Audit Protocol (CEAP) is a methodological perspective and critical synthesis for black-box AI evaluation. It addresses a recurring inferential problem: observable AI behavior is often used to support stronger claims about capabilities, internal states, mechanisms, robustness, or latent properties without making explicit which competing explanations the evaluation actually distinguishes. CEAP introduces a reusable contrastive reporting layer organized around a claim–interface–alternative triple ((C,T,\mathcal H)), where (C) is the target claim, (T) is the observational or interventional interface, and (\mathcal H) is the declared space of claim-relevant alternatives. The protocol requires evaluators to specify the target claim, identify claim-opposing alternatives, state the discriminatory role of each central test, audit dependence among evidence sources, report residual ambiguity, define a claim ceiling, and identify the next discriminating experimental need. title: Because Data Happens. FAIR data, infrastructure and AI for data-driven biodiversity research. Presentation by SciLifeLab Data Centre.
abstract: Slides from an invited presentation delivered at the Evolutionary Biology Centre (EBC), Uppsala University, on 15 September 2026. The talk introduces researchers in evolution, biodiversity and related fields to the data management support, infrastructure and services offered by the SciLifeLab Data Centre and the NBIS Data Management team, framed around FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles and Open Science. Structured along the research data life cycle — the presentation covers: why good research data management and metadata matter for biodiversity data; FAIR and metadata standards; Data Management Plans and the Data Stewardship Wizard (DSW); Swedish and international infrastructure for biodiversity data; SciLifeLab services (Data Repository/FigShare instance, Serve, Protocols, FAIR Storage, RDM Guidelines); compute and storage through NAISS; the tension between open sharing and data protection for sensitive species observations; the role of AI in data-driven biodiversity research; and available training and bioinformatics support.

title: Momentum Reflections with a Complex Native Source: Exact field symmetries and an obstruction to a real native basis
abstract: This technical note derives exact coordinate-reflection symmetries for a reciprocal lattice field Hamiltonian with a complex, finite-dimensional native source. The field reflection preserves the lattice-divergence constraint and transforms the complete interacting operator. Combined with two native half-period symmetries, it reduces the ground-energy momentum search to a region occupying one thirty-second of the momentum torus. Two exact trace identities give a separate obstruction: the specified native Hamiltonian and hopping involutions cannot share a real basis. They also exclude the individually signed native antiunitary symmetry considered here. At a reflection-fixed global momentum minimum, a normal ground vector can be chosen with joint reflection parity; the three reduced current-response vectors then occupy orthogonal sectors. This last conclusion retains its stated minimum and domain hypotheses. Significance within Recognition Science. The result supplies exact constraints on the full interacting candidate used in the RS particle-spectrum program, improves the conditional current-response estimate, and eliminates a proposed native real-basis shortcut. title: The Futures We Imagined, the Intelligence Between Us; A Science-Faction" From Capek Moravec's Czech Robots to Inter-Intelligence: An Annotated Bibliography of Predictions, Surprises and Possibilities
abstract: What did earlier thinkers anticipate about artificial intelligence, and what becomes visible only through living with it? Beginning with Hans Moravec’s forecasts of machine intelligence, this essay traces connections among Karel Čapek’s artificial workers, Pierre Teilhard de Chardin’s noosphere, Marshall McLuhan’s global village and Roy Ascott’s telematic art. Norbert Wiener’s account of responsibility, Edwin Hutchins’s distributed cognition and N. Katherine Hayles’s work on embodiment and cognitive assemblages provide complementary perspectives on contemporary human–AI relationships. The discussion distinguishes broad historical anticipations from specific developments in language models, automated intellectual work and feedback between human behavior and machine learning. It develops inter-intelligence as a framework for investigating what emerges through encounters among heterogeneous human, artificial and other living intelligences, without assuming equivalent capacities, consciousness or reciprocal experience. title: A laboratory method for AI-assisted science: formal proof, exact arithmetic, controlled experiment, and a claim ledger, tested for a month on the Navier-Stokes problem
abstract: Large language models produce mathematics and physics that read well and are sometimes wrong, and the discipline that has grown up around them is verification: proof assistants for proofs, and now public registries that check whether a repository proves what it claims. That discipline is necessary and it stops at the proof. This paper describes a working method that extends verifier-in-the-loop practice to the whole of a laboratory's loop -- choosing questions, building instruments, reading numbers, writing and publishing -- and reports what it did over one month in two small laboratories working on the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations: one running the method in full on a machine-checked programme for the frequency-truncated system, the other auditing an AI-generated, Lean-certified blow-up proof and arriving independently at two of the same instruments. title: Harness Evidence Worksheet for AI Supplier Assessment
abstract: A fillable worksheet for locating evidence about the harness component of an AI validation boundary during supplier assessment in regulated life sciences. Existing supplier questionnaires and management-system standards cover model provenance, vendor governance, change control, and security attestation. They say comparatively little about the engineered layer around the model — retrieval and context assembly, orchestration and tool routing, model invocation, output validation, telemetry, and failure response — where much of a probabilistic system's behavior is determined. The worksheet has five parts. The sponsor first declares the context of use, the model and how it is supplied, the configuration under assessment, and the human-in-the-loop arrangement. A standalone question set is then issued to the vendor. Responses are recorded in a grid of harness elements, each assigned an ownership state: sponsor, vendor, split, unassigned, or not applicable. The worksheet locates evidence and records ownership. It does not assess sufficiency, verify vendor claims, or constitute validation evidence. title: Novas tecnologias em investigação criminal: o uso da inteligência artificial.
abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) into public security, criminal investigation and forensic science is changing the way large volumes of data are collected, organized, correlated and interpreted. This study presents a literature review on the main applications of AI in criminal investigation, focusing on facial recognition, image and video analysis, human identification, forensic genetics, toxicology, digital forensics, crime pattern analysis and decision support. The review was based on indexed scientific literature and systematic and scoping reviews published in specialized journals, prioritizing recent studies and reference works on artificial intelligence, machine learning and forensic sciences. The findings indicate that AI can increase the speed of evidence screening, assist in pattern identification and support experts in repetitive or highly complex tasks. However, the literature also highlights limitations related to the quality and representativeness of databases, external validation, explainability, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, data protection and the need for human oversight. title: Advancements in Spatial Data Acquisition
abstract: Remote sensing techniques play a pivotal role in environmental monitoring, observation, and management as they allow for the systematic, large-scale, and long-term observation of Earth's surface without physical contact. In the digital age, remote sensing facilitates time-series analysis and cost-effective monitoring while preserving natural habitats. Various advanced technologies, including Hyperspectral Imaging, LiDAR, Photogrammetry, UAVs, and SAR, are employed to formulate strategies for environmental risk mitigation and sustainable resource management. Additionally, the integration of multi-sensor data with AI and real-time cloud processing improves decision-making in environmental assessments and governance. Moreover, the fusion of multi-sensor data, supported by AI-driven analytics and real-time cloud processing, enhances decision-making capabilities in environmental risk assessment, resource management, and early warning systems, which contributes to more sustainable environmental governance. title: Data‐Driven Journeys
abstract: The growing challenges of urban congestion, ageing populations, and environmental sustainability in Japan demand innovative transportation solutions. This chapter explores how spatial data science and big data analytics can transform sustainable transportation planning. It highlights Japan's complex transportation issues, including accessibility for vulnerable populations and disaster resilience, and proposes a Data-Driven Active Transportation Model. This model integrates real-time traffic data, geographic information systems (GIS), and advanced analytics to optimise walking and cycling zones, aiming to reduce congestion and emissions while improving mobility for all users. A systematic literature review across databases such as JSTOR, Google Scholar, and SpringerLink critically examined 133 studies to identify trends, gaps, and opportunities in Japan's transportation landscape. Findings reveal a paradigm shift towards intelligent transport systems (ITS), Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS), and the integration of AI and IoT within the Society 5.0 framework. title: The Futures We Imagined, the Intelligence Between Us; A Science-Faction" From Capek Moravec's Czech Robots to Inter-Intelligence: An Annotated Bibliography of Predictions, Surprises and Possibilities
abstract: What did earlier thinkers anticipate about artificial intelligence, and what becomes visible only through living with it? Beginning with Hans Moravec’s forecasts of machine intelligence, this essay traces connections among Karel Čapek’s artificial workers, Pierre Teilhard de Chardin’s noosphere, Marshall McLuhan’s global village and Roy Ascott’s telematic art. Norbert Wiener’s account of responsibility, Edwin Hutchins’s distributed cognition and N. Katherine Hayles’s work on embodiment and cognitive assemblages provide complementary perspectives on contemporary human–AI relationships. The discussion distinguishes broad historical anticipations from specific developments in language models, automated intellectual work and feedback between human behavior and machine learning. It develops inter-intelligence as a framework for investigating what emerges through encounters among heterogeneous human, artificial and other living intelligences, without assuming equivalent capacities, consciousness or reciprocal experience. title: Harness Evidence Worksheet for AI Supplier Assessment
abstract: A fillable worksheet for locating evidence about the harness component of an AI validation boundary during supplier assessment in regulated life sciences. Existing supplier questionnaires and management-system standards cover model provenance, vendor governance, change control, and security attestation. They say comparatively little about the engineered layer around the model — retrieval and context assembly, orchestration and tool routing, model invocation, output validation, telemetry, and failure response — where much of a probabilistic system's behavior is determined. The worksheet has five parts. The sponsor first declares the context of use, the model and how it is supplied, the configuration under assessment, and the human-in-the-loop arrangement. A standalone question set is then issued to the vendor. Responses are recorded in a grid of harness elements, each assigned an ownership state: sponsor, vendor, split, unassigned, or not applicable. The worksheet locates evidence and records ownership. It does not assess sufficiency, verify vendor claims, or constitute validation evidence. title: Claim–Evidence Audit Protocol (CEAP) A Contrastive Reporting Layer for Black-Box AI Evaluation
abstract: The Claim–Evidence Audit Protocol (CEAP) is a methodological perspective and critical synthesis for black-box AI evaluation. It addresses a recurring inferential problem: observable AI behavior is often used to support stronger claims about capabilities, internal states, mechanisms, robustness, or latent properties without making explicit which competing explanations the evaluation actually distinguishes. CEAP introduces a reusable contrastive reporting layer organized around a claim–interface–alternative triple ((C,T,\mathcal H)), where (C) is the target claim, (T) is the observational or interventional interface, and (\mathcal H) is the declared space of claim-relevant alternatives. The protocol requires evaluators to specify the target claim, identify claim-opposing alternatives, state the discriminatory role of each central test, audit dependence among evidence sources, report residual ambiguity, define a claim ceiling, and identify the next discriminating experimental need. title: The Terrorism Enablement Triangle: A conceptual model of intent, capability and resources in an era of AI-augmented threats
abstract: Terrorism assessments have long paired intent with capability, while threat and opportunity models add situational conditions and structured professional judgement frameworks address engagement, resources and protective factors. This paper proposes the Terrorism Enablement Triangle (TET), a conceptual model that treats intent, capability and resources as three interacting actor-centred dimensions of terrorist-action feasibility, with opportunity as the surrounding operating environment. A structured conceptual review identifies relevant prior art in threat triangles, engagement–intent–capability frameworks, crime-science opportunity models and resource-mobilisation accounts. TET’s contribution is a bounded re-specification: it distinguishes an actor’s competence from the assets available to them and separates beliefs, grievances and engagement from violent intent, mobilisation and action. The paper examines three possible ways AI could affect enablement: influence on intent through personalised interaction, capability uplift through task assistance, and resource compression through automation or reduced time, labour and specialist input. It proposes questions for empirical testing.

title: Designing a Research-Service Entity for Frontier AI
abstract: This registration establishes a timestamped, immutable record of a working paper analyzing the structural conflict of interest that arises when frontier AI providers simultaneously serve as scientific infrastructure and as competitors in the research frontier their infrastructure enables. Using the September 2026 Navier–Stokes episode as a stylized case (taking no position on its disputed facts), the paper argues that the resulting problem is one of verifiability, not virtue: when a provider controls the model, the logs, the data flows, and a competing research program, its assurance that it did not use a researcher's work cannot be independently checked. title: Surviving the 2050 Extinction Deadline
abstract: Theoretical physics shows that the universe is stranger than the wildest science fiction. Two-and-half thousand years ago, the Chinese historian Lao Zi reported the science of a civilization that was already ancient at his time. Those Ancients proposed a sophisticated sum-zero creation theory that explains the principle of the universe and its restoring force. They concluded that the immutable laws of the universe (physics) condition the behaviour of humanity (psychology). Unfortunately, their warnings were mystified. As a result, humanity developed Systemic-Mental-Failure, which caused humanmade extinction threats such as climate change and nuclear war. Education, science, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) maintain that failure by promoting consensus-based information, which fosters static thinking in a hyperdynamic tech-reality. In 2024, Antonio Guterres warned that 2050 is the year of no return for climate change. His warning fosters the global hoarding of critical resources, which could evoke a nuclear conflict far before that deadline. title: Eye in the Sky
abstract: Eye in the Sky: explore how modern Earth-observation constellations, sensors, and analytics deliver actionable, scalable environmental intelligence. It traces the evolution from Landsat and NOAA heritage to today's public–private fleets, and reports a 2015–2024 bibliometric pulse mapping of leading countries, disciplines, and document types. The chapter explains multispectral and hyperspectral imaging, SAR, LiDAR, and thermal infrared, showing how fused data quantify vegetation condition, soil moisture, land-use change, wildfires, floods, sea level, and greenhouse gases. It examines the accelerating integration of AI/ML with GIS/ GPS for classification, prediction, and anomaly detection, while addressing technical, economic, legal, and ethical constraints on access, processing, and privacy. Forward-looking guidance recommends interoperable standards, explainable models, advances in nanosatellite propulsion, open tooling, and crisis-time data-sharing compacts to democratize high-resolution evidence for policy and practice. The result is an editor's roadmap to trustworthy, timely, and equitable satellite-enabled environmental stewardship, grounded in rigorous science and operational

title: A laboratory method for AI-assisted science: formal proof, exact arithmetic, controlled experiment, and a claim ledger, tested for a month on the Navier-Stokes problem
abstract: Large language models produce mathematics and physics that read well and are sometimes wrong, and the discipline that has grown up around them is verification: proof assistants for proofs, and now public registries that check whether a repository proves what it claims. That discipline is necessary and it stops at the proof. This paper describes a working method that extends verifier-in-the-loop practice to the whole of a laboratory's loop -- choosing questions, building instruments, reading numbers, writing and publishing -- and reports what it did over one month in two small laboratories working on the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations: one running the method in full on a machine-checked programme for the frequency-truncated system, the other auditing an AI-generated, Lean-certified blow-up proof and arriving independently at two of the same instruments. title: Preserving Person‐Centred Fundamental Care in Human‐ AI Collaboration: A Scoping Review
abstract: AIM: To map and synthesize evidence on Human-AI Collaboration (HAIC) in nursing and community care contexts guided by the Fundamentals of Care (FoC) framework DESIGN: Scoping Review. DATA SOURCES: Multiple databases including PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL and PsycArticles were searched for articles published between January 2020 and July 2025. METHODS: Studies involving care providers or recipients collaborating with AI in nursing or community care contexts were included. Hospital-based diagnostic and non-empirical studies were excluded. REPORTING METHOD: The JBI updated nine-step framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines were followed. RESULTS: In total 1744 articles were retrieved, of which 26 were included in this review. Three configurations of the triadic caring relationship were identified: provider-mediated, joint engagement and recipient-facing configurations. The HAIC tasks concentrated on physical care, while the integration of physical, psychosocial, and relational care remained limited. title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) - Based Driven technique for Marking and Grading of Essay Handwriting Examination Scripts in Tertiary Institution
abstract: Manual grading of essay handwritten examination scripts is time-consuming, subject to grader fatigue, and prone to interrater inconsistency, particularly when class size is large.This study addressed these challenges by proposing an AI-based technique for marking and grading essay handwritten examination scripts, using a deterministic rule-based engine for multiple choice questions (MCQ) alongside a Gemini 2.5 Flash large language model guided by structured prompts and marking rubrics for theory questions.A two-phase model converted physical handwritten scripts into digital structure for AI evaluation, while a multi-strategy javaScript object notation (JSON) parsing approach extracted and validated structured data using natural language processing (NLP) and deep learning methods.The paper adopted a tri-instance pipeline handling marking-guide extraction and handwritten script transcription for grading, evaluated against human-expert scores using a double-blind design to eliminate anchoring and confirmation bias.The system was tested on forty (40) handwritten scripts, twenty (20) from CSC 307 (Compiler Construction) and twenty (20) from CSC 405 ("Computer Graphics"), collected from

title: DIGITAL DIVIDE IN MATERNAL TELEHEALTH: EQUITY GAPS IN PRENATAL AND POSTPARTUM REMOTE CARE
abstract: The rapid expansion of telehealth in prenatal and postpartum care has been widely promoted as a means of improving access to maternal health services, yet its equity implications remain insufficiently understood. This paper presents a narrative review synthesizing current evidence on equity gaps in maternal telehealth across six domains: racial and ethnic disparities, rural and infrastructural barriers, global perspectives from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), the mental health-specific digital divide, language- and immigration-related barriers, and equity implications of emerging AI-driven maternal health tools. A literature search was conducted across PubMed, Google Scholar, and Web of Science for peer-reviewed articles and institutional reports published between 2015 and 2026, yielding 39 sources. Findings reveal a consistent "digital-first" paradox: telehealth adoption frequently follows pre-existing lines of digital advantage, in some cases widening rather than narrowing disparities in the timeliness and continuity of care for Black, Hispanic, rural, immigrant, and lower-income patients, and LMIC populations. title: Interspecies Communication and the Problems of Translation
abstract: Across law and science, interspecies translation has emerged as a consequential aspiration: from legal efforts to grant rights to animals and rivers, to AI-powered attempts to decode cetacean communication through bioacoustic machine learning. I examine the Cetacean Translation Initiative (Project CETI) as a case study in the constitution of such aspirations, arguing that AI-assisted interspecies translation constitutes the parties to the relation it purports to mediate. Situating Project CETI alongside the ‘rights of nature’ movement, I trace the linguistic presuppositions underlying approaches to language as an engineering problem divorced from semantics, an inheritance running from Shannon and Weaver to contemporary Large Language Models. I then demonstrate how the Generative Adversarial Networks Project CETI deploys perform communication in ways that are normatively constitutive. The technical novelty of AI and the normative novelty of Rights of Nature converge in a single operation: AI-assisted interspecies translation performs the parties whose encounter it mediates.

title: EARLY DETECTION OF ENDOMETRIOSIS – A LITERATURE REVIEW OF DIAGNOSTIC METHODS AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
abstract: Research objectives: Endometriosis is a chronic disease that impairs the daily functioning and quality of life of many women. This literature review summarizes current diagnostic methods for endometriosis, their advantages and limitations, and discusses emerging approaches, particularly established and emerging imaging techniques. Scope of review: Relevant publications were identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and other scientific databases. This literature review focused on studies published between 2020 and 2025 that addressed established and emerging diagnostic approaches for endometriosis, including imaging techniques, biomarkers, and artificial intelligence. Findings: Endometriosis commonly presents with chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility. Current evidence indicates that imaging plays a central role in diagnosis. Transvaginal ultrasound remains the first-line imaging modality, while magnetic resonance imaging provides complementary information for disease staging and assessment of complex cases. title: Marc analític predictiu per a l'evaluació del risc creditici i la mitigació de biaixos algorítmics
abstract: [EN] As the financial sector increasingly adopts Machine Learning (ML) for credit scoring, the industry faces a critical tension between predictive accuracy, algorithmic bias, and regulatory transparency. The primary objective of this project is to design, develop, and evaluate a predictive analytics framework for loan eligibility that actively mitigates algorithmic bias while maintaining high classification performance. Unlike standard implementations, this research does not solely treat credit scoring as a binary classification problem, but as an ethical engineering challenge. Utilizing a simulated credit risk dataset, the study evaluates advanced ensemble methods against traditional linear baselines. The final optimized XGBoost model achieves an exceptional AUC of 0.9477, proving capable of learning minority class patterns without requiring synthetic oversampling techniques like SMOTE. Consequently, this project delivers three main contributions to the field of ethical FinTech. title: Integrating vr/ar, arduino and ai-supported personalisation in lower-secondary stem education: evidence, risks and implications
abstract: This article presents a structured narrative review of three technologies that are increasingly integrated into STEM education at the lower-secondary level: virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR), open-source microcontroller platforms of the Arduino type, and personalisation supported by artificial intelligence (AI). The review is guided by three questions, concerning the available evidence, the reported risks, and the pedagogical conditions for responsible implementation. It draws on peer-reviewed studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses indexed in Scopus and Web of Science, as well as on reports of international and national organisations (UNESCO, the European Commission, the OECD and the Bulgarian Ministry of Education and Science). The evidence on motivation, engagement and learning outcomes is summarised together with its limitations – health and age constraints, cognitive overload and the novelty effect, data protection, the digital divide, and a thin evidence base. The review proposes an integrative, pedagogy-centred model and draws conclusions for the design of a future empirical study. title: Effectiveness of Electronic Health and Wellness Coaching (e-Coaching) in improving psychological well-being in third-level students- Systematic Review (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Levels of psychological distress amongst students have been increasing; however, individual and institutional barriers may limit access to timely support. Electronic health and wellness coaching (e-coaching) is emerging as a potential approach to increase access to structured, interactive psychological support, but its effectiveness, user engagement and longer-term sustainability among third-level students remains unclear. OBJECTIVE To synthesise evidence on the effectiveness of e-coaching for improving psychological well-being and reducing psychological distress in third-level students; and to examine the sustainability of effects, engagement and adherence, and relevant coaching characteristics. METHODS Electronic databases, CINAHL, PubMed, PsycINFO, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase and ProQuest were searched with no limits on publication year. Studies meeting the inclusion criteria: students aged ≥18 years enrolled in third-level education and evaluated a digitally delivered intervention incorporating human, peer, automated or artificial intelligence supported coaching, were included. title: Artificial Intelligence and Behavioural Approaches to Human Body Donation: A Scoping Review of Determinants, Predictive Methods, Interventions, Policy and Implementation
abstract: Human body donation is an important component of medical education, anatomical research and surgical skills training. Cadaveric dissection provides medical students with direct exposure to human anatomy, while donated human bodies may also support postgraduate surgical education and procedural training. Despite its educational and scientific importance, many institutions and countries experience an imbalance between the availability of donated bodies and educational requirements. The determinants of willingness to donate one's body are complex and multifactorial. Previous research has identified demographic, psychological, social, cultural and religious factors associated with attitudes toward body donation. Factors such as knowledge and awareness, altruism, trust in institutions, family support, concerns regarding respectful treatment of the body, religious beliefs, cultural practices and perceptions of the donation process may influence willingness to donate. title: The Formalized Science Transition: From AGI-Driven Discovery to Verified Scientific Knowledge
abstract: Advanced AI or AGI is usually evaluated as a reasoning system whose outputs remain the primary object of trust. This paper examines a different possibility: sufficiently capable AI may act as an epistemic bootstrapper that moves some scientific reasoning from transient model outputs into persistent, machine-checkable infrastructure. Recent work already demonstrates several prerequisites: scientific theories have been formalized in Lean, AI-assisted formalization has reached research-level mathematics and physics, and formalization has exposed substantive errors in published physics. FST develops four claims: scientific trust should be separated into deductive, empirical and specification trust; empirical status should be versioned separately from logical validity; the proposed transition should make a measurable supply-to-demand prediction; and its stopping points should be classified by cause. title: Practical Semantic Interoperability recommendations for the EOSC Federation
abstract: As the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) evolves into a federation of autonomous nodes (EOSC Federation), semantic interoperability is essential to ensure that research data and metadata are consistently understood by both humans and machines across diverse systems and disciplines. This document establishes practical recommendations intended for semantic professionals of EOSC Nodes and the EOSC Federation, with one recommendation also for the EOSC Association, based on the analysis of the current status in the Landscape Overview for the EOSC Federation Semantic Interoperability in 2025. The main goal of the recommendations is to achieve semantic interoperability across the federation of EOSC Nodes on the level of datasets, metadata, mappings, catalogues, validation and governance. title: kgsteward: a tool for building, reproducing and maintaining distributed knowledge graphs
abstract: Collaborative research projects in life sciences increasingly need to integrate private, embargoed consortium data with public reference databases in order to reach statistically meaningful interpretations. The Resource Description Framework (RDF) is well suited to this task: it facilitates the integration of heterogeneous data sources, and allows researchers to keep data and their documentation as metadata in the same place, provided the knowledge graph itself remains private during the time course of the project. Nevertheless, the development and long-term maintenance of a scientific knowledge graph remains a challenging, labour-intensive endeavour owing to the state of constant flux of most public resources. To tackle this challenge, we present kgsteward, a Python command-line tool that builds and maintains knowledge graphs inside RDF stores from a single, version-controlled configuration file. kgsteward supports multiple triplestores, keeps the local graph up-to-date with its external sources possibly already in RDF, or transformed into it on the fly, and uses SPARQL 1.1 UPDATE commands to amend further imported RDF on the fly. title: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Wearable Technologies for Predicting Functional Decline and Supporting Rehabilitation and Independent Living in Adults with Physical Disabilities: A Systematic Review and Translational Framework for Saudi Arabia
abstract: Abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) and wearable sensors are increasingly capable of quantifying mobility, gait, balance, upper-limb activity, physiological status, and rehabilitation dose outside conventional clinical encounters. title: The Formalized Science Transition: From AGI-Driven Discovery to Verified Scientific Knowledge
abstract: Advanced AI or AGI is usually evaluated as a reasoning system whose outputs remain the primary object of trust. This paper examines a different possibility: sufficiently capable AI may act as an epistemic bootstrapper that moves some scientific reasoning from transient model outputs into persistent, machine-checkable infrastructure. Recent work already demonstrates several prerequisites: scientific theories have been formalized in Lean, AI-assisted formalization has reached research-level mathematics and physics, and formalization has exposed substantive errors in published physics. FST develops four claims: scientific trust should be separated into deductive, empirical and specification trust; empirical status should be versioned separately from logical validity; the proposed transition should make a measurable supply-to-demand prediction; and its stopping points should be classified by cause. title: Acceptance of AI-Based Assistive Technologies for Autonomy Support Among Older Adults: A Scoping Review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Population aging is leading to increased demand for health and long-term care. AI-based assistive technologies have been developed to support autonomy and care for older adults, yet real‑world adoption remains limited. We review evidence on acceptance and determinants of acceptance of AI‑based assistive technologies among older adults. METHODS: We conducted a scoping review using the JBI methodology and followed PRISMA‑ScR guidelines for reporting. Four databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane) were searched for studies published from January 2010 to June 2025, initially in any language. We included studies examining acceptance and determinants of acceptance of AI-based assistive technologies among adults aged 65 years and older. We synthesized data using inductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Twenty‑nine studies met the inclusion criteria, with over one-third conducted in Europe (n = 10). Overall attitudes toward AI‑based assistive technologies were generally favorable when technologies were perceived as useful, easy to use, and tailored to needs. However, actual use was low. abstract: As the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) evolves into a federation of autonomous nodes (EOSC Federation), semantic interoperability is essential to ensure that research data and metadata are consistently understood by both humans and machines across diverse systems and disciplines. This document establishes practical recommendations intended for semantic professionals of EOSC Nodes and the EOSC Federation, with one recommendation also for the EOSC Association, based on the analysis of the current status in the Landscape Overview for the EOSC Federation Semantic Interoperability in 2025. title: AI-GRACE: A Use-Case Operationalization Framework for Agentic AI: From Organizational Objectives and Obligations to Deployment Capabilities and Architecture
abstract: Organizations deploying agentic artificial intelligence must determine more than whether a model is trustworthy; they must establish what to validate, control, and observe for a use case to deliver its intended outcome while meeting applicable obligations. This paper proposes AI-GRACE (Agentic Intelligence-Governance, Risk, Assurance, Controls, and Evidence) as a use-case operationalization framework connecting organizational governance with technical implementation. The proposal draws on professional observations and a purposive synthesis of standards and literature, using design science to frame the method contribution and situational method engineering to guide contextual tailoring and reuse. The framework establishes objectives and obligations and then assesses risks in seven proposed domains, including mission and value realization. It derives requirements for assurance before deployment, runtime controls, and evidence, which guide capability qualification, gap assessment, and a logical architecture.
